articleTitle: Design of Optimized Carry Select Adder (OCSA) for Low-Power IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This work demonstrates the design of a low-power circuit for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Most of the IoT and embedded applications relies on battery powered devices and executes high-speed computation. Hence, power constraints are critical. Adders are the crucial component for any computation unit. Thus, the design of low-power and high-speed arithmetic processing units are in growing demand for extended battery life and efficient computation in IoT devices. In this paper we proposed the architecture of a Carry Select Adder (CSA) optimized to reduce power and propagation delay. The architecture employs MDCVSL (Modified Differential Cascode Voltage-Switch Logic) as a Mux to realize efficient computation and minimum Power-Delay Product (PDP). The proposed Optimized Carry Select Adder (OCSA) architecture is implemented in Cadence Virtuso using GMDK 90 and the result shows that it improves power and propagation delay by a factor of $\mathbf{2 0 \%} \& \mathbf{1 0 . 5 2 \%}$ respectively.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Feed forward ANN Architectures Based Wind Speed Prediction for India
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Predicting wind speed (WS) is essential for evaluating energy resources, especially when it comes to maximizing wind turbine performance and minimizing environmental effects. This study modelswind speed as a function of several meteorological characteristics for Indian sites using machine learning techniques, with an emphasis on Feed forward Neural Network with varying hidden layers and dropout mechanisms. The accuracy is evaluated by evaluation metric. It is found that Feed forward Neural Network with dropout mechanisms is important for WS prediction for Indian site. The findings provide a foundation for future research to explore advanced ANN techniques and hybrid models to further enhance prediction accuracy and support renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Investigation of hydrogen recirculation ratios in individual ejectors under various operating conditions for a 110 kW PEMFC
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Ejectors, characterized by a simple structure and zero parasitic power consumption, are reliable hydrogen supply mechanisms for fuel cells. Nevertheless, the ejector’s recirculation performance is typically inadequate under low power conditions, with variations in operating variables influencing its operating range. To mitigate this limitation, the present study examines the effects of three key operating variables—primary flow inlet temperature, secondary flow inlet temperature, and secondary flow water vapor mass fraction—on the recirculation ratio. The study compares hydrogen recirculation ratios under both rated and expanded operating conditions. Within the power range of 20 to 110 kW, the total recirculation ratio exhibits a slight increase with primary inlet temperatures rising from $\mathbf{2 8 0}$ to 340 K and a slight decrease as secondary inlet temperatures escalate from 320 to 370 K. With secondary inlet pressure held constant for a given stack power, an increase in secondary inlet temperature may decrease the fluid’s average density. An increase in water vapor mass fraction from $\mathbf{3 0 \%}$ to $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ leads to a substantial rise in the total recirculation ratio. However, the hydrogen recirculation ratio experiences a marked decrease of $\mathbf{7 6. 2 2 \%}$ at 60 kW and $75.47 \%$ at 20 kW. Maintaining the secondary flow water vapor mass fraction at or below $\mathbf{3 0 \%}$ effectively guarantees a hydrogen recirculation ratio of at least 0.5 across the $20-110 \mathrm{~kW}$ power range.

articleTitle: A CPW Fed Dual Band High Frequency Antenna for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile antenna suitable for 5G applications and Internet of Things (IoT) devices with the height of $\mathbf{0. 2 5 4} \mathrm{mm}$ (about $0.0030 \lambda$) and with tiny dimensions of 15 mm X 40 mm (about $0.18 \lambda \times 0.48 \lambda$) is designed and analyzed. The frequency range that the antenna radiating is from 3 GHz to 6 GHz. The proposed antenna is designed to meet the stringent requirements of modern wireless communication systems, which include high efficiency, broad bandwidth, and small size. We recommend low-profile CPW (Co-planar Wave-guide) antenna with 0.254 mm thick to reduce power loss. The CPW antenna consists of an asymmetric inverted F-shaped radiating slot, a feed line and a top ground. The recommended tri-band antenna is easy to use. Plotting the suggested antenna versus the operating frequency reveals an extremely high efficiency of over $95 \%$ with the Gain 3.45 dBi is used for 5G network applications operating at dual-band.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of P&O MPPT Technique for PV Panel and Array Integration with Boost Converter: An Analytical and MATLAB Simulation Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The energy radiated from sun is one of the best nonconventional resources as it produces clean energy to generate electricity. PV panels are utilized to convert energy radiated from the sun is converted in to the electrical energy. The proposed paper suggests the mathematical modelling of solar panel and. This mathematical modeling is implemented in MATLAB simulation. This mathematical modeling is simulated under different to get standard test condition of the panel. The environmental conditions are changes continuously, so working points shift from the point of MPP to the other location on the PV curve. In order to extract maximum power, it is necessary to design a controller. This paper shows the implementation of the Perturb and Observe (P&O) algorithm to trace MPP. In a simulation model of MPPT change in irradiation is considered and temperature remains unchanged.

articleTitle: Real-Time Smart Aquarium Monitoring System Driven by IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Aquaponics-based IoT-based organic farming is a cutting-edge solution to sustainable agriculture. The Smart Aquarium Monitoring System powered by IoT is designed to revolutionize aquarium management by providing real-time data acquisition and remote monitoring through a web interface or mobile application. The system integrates multiple sensors to continuously track crucial environmental factors, such as the temperature of the water and the surrounding air, humidity, Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) for water purity, and water level. Alerts are produced in the event of any deviations from set parameters, allowing users to take prompt corrective actions. To enhance functionality and sustainability, the system incorporates a solar panel with a Battery Management System (BMS) to power and charge the system’s batteries, ensuring reliable and eco-friendly operation. The ESP32 microcontroller serves as the central controller, managing data acquisition, processing, and communication between sensors and the application. Additionally, the system features the ESP32-CAM for live video monitoring, offering real-time visual insights. By automating temperature regulation and lighting, he system keeps ideal circumstances for aquatic life, reducing manual intervention and ensuring a stable habitat. This innovative approach leverages IoT technology to offer a user-friendly, efficient solution for aquarium management, enhancing both convenience and the health of aquatic organisms.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Managment in a Grid Connected PV System with Energy Storage Device
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Power management analysis in microgrid system is one of the important research areas in the recent age. In this paper, a PV integrated Grid sytem with energy storage back up is developed to analyze the power management. All the generating units and the battery is interconnected through different types of converters. The battery is used as backup enrgy source and it is operated when solar fails to generate and in the condition of low power generation. To keep the system stable and of high quality, an inverter controller must be used. To extract maximum power, the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) approach is also used. The suggested system uses the power management technique to control the correct operation of every unit and the power distribution between the grid and battery. It also effectively monitors the battery’s charge level while it is operating. To regulate the power flow, a bidirectional converter is linked to the battery. With the aid of an inverter, the DC output from the PV and battery is supplied to the grid and load. After the reference current is generated using PMA and a proportional integral controller (PI), all of the related converters switch. Through simulation, the suggested work’s efficacy is confirmed.

articleTitle: Enhancement in High Resistance Fault Detection using Quadrilateral Relay for Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Power transmission lines are essential in any power system. The security of transmission structures continues to be a challenging issue due to supply costs and reliability. Occasionally, numerous types of faults may arise on the transmission line, resulting in significant fluctuations in fault characteristics. This work aims to examine the identification of line-to-ground faults, line-to-line faults, high resistance faults (HRF), and external line-to-ground faults in transmission lines. Additionally, a distance relay is designed with Quadrilateral attributes. Line fault detection is accomplished via the signaling of currents and voltages. The FFT analysis is employed to ascertain the phasor values of recorded electrical signals. Later using sequence filters, the phasor is transformed into three sequence components. After that, the resistance and reactance of the faulted line are computed for various categories of faults. PSACD software is utilized to simulate the considered power system. In the event of close-in faults occurring in grid-connected transmission lines, a distance relay including Quadrilateral characteristics is utilized. Numerous fault conditions arise from significant parameter fluctuations, including high resistance and exterior line-to-ground faults. The proposed relay trigger in the event of a fault at various positions of transmission line.

articleTitle: High-Gain Switched-Capacitor based Novel DC-DC Converter for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The increased adoption of renewable energy has driven research for converters that offer reliable way to integrate low-voltage dc input from photovoltaic (PV) and fuel cell based systems. In this context, a basic voltage lift-cell and a Switched Capacitor (SC) network are integrated in this study to present a non-isolated converter architecture. This integration results in a single-switch, single-inductor structure with reduced component count, high conversion ratio, and reduced stress across semiconductor devices. The novel converter is analyzed in continuous (CCM) and discontinuous (DCM) conduction modes and simulation results are presented using MATLAB/Simulink software with 48 V input voltage, $75 \%$ duty cycle, and switching frequency of 75 kHz. An analytical efficiency analysis along with simulation using PLECS software is presented. A detailed comparison study reveals that the enhanced voltage gain and decreased voltage stresses with reduced component count are significant features of the proposed converter. Detailed experimental findings are ultimately gathered to support the workability of the novel dc-dc converter.

articleTitle: Assessing State-Wise Policy Frameworks for Electric Vehicle Adoption: Transportation Sector in India
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The rapid growth of the transportation sector has led to significant challenges in terms of environmental sustainability and energy security. Electric vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a promising solution to mitigate these challenges by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. This paper focuses on analyzing the policy measures and their implications for state-wise electric vehicle adoption in India. India, as a signatory to global climate agreements, has set ambitious targets for EV adoption to combat air pollution and reduce its carbon footprint. However, the adoption of EVs across different states in India is influenced by various factors, including infrastructure development, economic conditions, consumer awareness, and policy support. This study conducts a comprehensive review of the policies and incentives the central and state governments provide to promote EV adoption. This paper also highlights the policy initiatives such as financial incentives, tax exemptions, subsidies, and charging infrastructure development.

articleTitle: Model-Based Control for Enhanced Headlamp Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper follows a model-based design approach for the closed-loop headlamp control system, primarily with the purpose of improving luminance control as well as the efficiency of energy consumption in automotive applications. The method is centered around a DC-DC boost converter with high output voltage accuracy to ensure optimal power transfer towards headlamps. It can be directly developed in MATLAB/Simulink, which allows faster prototyping and algorithm testing before hardware is even deployed. The closed-loop feedback mechanism continuously compares output voltage to a setpoint and dynamically adjusts the duty cycle of the converter in real-time to maintain uniform lighting. In addition, the converter is validated through simulation to have stable voltage regulation with minimal overshoot and fast settling times. The hardware implementation of the system is carried out using an STM Nucleo board, which brings the reliability of the Simulink model into practical and real-time implementation. This paper indicates that model-based design offers a proper way of optimizing development time thereby ensuring robust headlamp performance under variable conditions.

articleTitle: Power Quality Enhancement in Electric Vehicle-Integrated Distribution Systems using a Solar-Powered Dynamic Voltage Restorer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The increasing use of electric vehicles (EVs) has led to significant concerns regarding power quality due to nonlinear loads, heavy load switching, and line faults. To address these issues, a three-phase bridge inverter, acting as a dynamic voltage restorer (DVR), is powered by a solar-powered DC-DC converter. The DVR operates in synchronization with the distribution system, effectively mitigating power quality problems. By injecting compensating voltage from the alternate source into the main grid, the DVR recovers voltage sags caused by EV charging and other disturbances. To maximize solar panel output, the system incorporates the Perturb and Observe (P&O) algorithm. The entire system is modeled and simulated using MATLAB/Simulink, with results demonstrating that the proposed system performs efficiently in restoring power quality during voltage sag events in EV-integrated distribution systems.

articleTitle: Measurement of Light Response in Luminescent Solar Concentrators
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: In this paper we have designed and developed the device for the characterization of Luminescent Solar Concentrators (LSCs), Which can precisely measure the optical properties of the LSC Slab. Encountering the limitation of the derived technologies, the existing technologies use the integrating Spheres and complex setup to characterize the material which has limited to precise measurement of light emitting from the edges of the LSCs. This particular system incorporates photodiodes with an Arduino to measure light emerging from the edges of LSCs and offer precise and optimal characterization. This setup simplifies the testing process, enhances measurement accuracy, and provides detailed insights into the light conversion capabilities of LSCs. Overall, the precision enhancement and cost-effectiveness lead to improved advances and optical properties of the LSC devices. The outcome of the device gives details of the properties of the LSC applications.

articleTitle: A Review of Current Trends in Greenhouse Gas Emission Prediction through Machine Intelligence Learning Techniques and Future Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Increased GHG emissions from human activities have severe environmental and health impacts, making accurate predictions essential for effective mitigation strategies. This review explores various models for GHG emission prediction, focusing on ML DL techniques. It examines the contributions of sectors such as transportation, agriculture, and energy production, and discusses challenges in estimating emissions from sources like soils, livestock, and hydroelectric power. Prediction accuracy has significantly increased thanks to developments in ML and DL algorithms, such as RNNs, CNNs, and artificial neural networks (ANNs). Case studies highlight the effectiveness of these models in capturing complex emission patterns and informing emission reduction decisions. Integrating ML and DL with traditional environmental data analysis offers a comprehensive approach to GHG emission prediction, supporting sustainable development and climate change mitigation. Despite significant progress, further research is needed to enhance model interpretability, data integration, and real-time prediction capabilities to address the dynamic nature of GHG emissions and their global impact.

articleTitle: Awareness analysis of online peer-to-peer lending services amongst Indian MSMEs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Online peer to peer (P2P) lending is a form of digital lending that connects the borrowers and the lenders to help mobilize funds with the help of an online lending platform without the intermediation of traditional intermediaries such as banks. The empirical study aims to identify the awareness regarding the existence of p 2 p lending platforms amongst the Indian SMEs. The study used a self-structured questionnaire to collect the data on a sample of two hundred respondents. The findings of the study reveals that there is a limited awareness about the existence of P2P lending amongst Indian SMEs and majority of them are not even aware of the p 2 p lending as a mode of financing. Moreover, the awareness level varies based on Gender and location. The finding of the study have significant implications for the platform manager’s as it will increase their understanding about the current status of awareness about p 2 p lending amongst the SMEs which will help them to design specific marketing strategies to reach the large base of Indian SMEs. Additionally, the study will help regulators and policymakers frame the policies and regulations that will support the healthy development of peer-to-peer lending as a substitute source of funding for small and medium-sized enterprises.

articleTitle: Cyber Security Risk Analysis of IoT Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The application of IoT in integration with various other technologies has widened the attack surface and introduced security vulnerabilities which further make multifold challenges for the cyber security team. To handle these challenges a structured risk assessment is required to help the cyber security team to assess and mitigate the cyber security risk of IoT ecosystem. This paper studied various risk assessment techniques and found out that there is no risk assessment available for IoT ecosystem. This paper aims to prepare the novel unique risk assessment framework for IoT ecosystem named as RA-IoT. The outcome of the framework shall provide a unified, systematic, comprehensive, and structured risk register for IoT ecosystem. This framework shall help the cyber security teams to use the RA-IoT risk register as a tool for assessing and managing the cyber security risk of IoT ecosystem.

articleTitle: Step-by-Step Reliability Analysis of Wireless Battery Charger for Electric Vehicles using the Markov Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Literature has several wireless battery charger topologies, and, generally, their performance comparisons are made based on cost and efficiency. However, reliability even being a very crucial parameter is mostly overlooked. This research paper employs the Markov process (MP) based approach to conduct a comprehensive reliability analysis of wireless battery charging systems tailored specifically for electric vehicles (EVs). The research is focused on inductive coupling wireless power transfer, which is widely used due to its efficiency and compatibility with existing EV infrastructure. Firstly, to analyze the reliability of WBC, two topologies, which are being intensively studied in the literature, are selected. Thereafter, the converters are designed for the same set of specifications. Then, with the known parameters, the reliability analysis is performed based on the MP. The process steps are elaborated in detail which can be utilized for the analysis of any power electronic converter. Finally, results are presented, and a discussion is made on the outcome of the study.

articleTitle: ADBS: Automatic Dynamic Braking System for Semi-autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an Autonomous Dynamic Braking System for vehicles that aims to increase road safety and ride comfort by preventing collisions. The proposed system analyses the driving condition and brakes the vehicle automatically if there is a chance of a collision using Time to Collision (TTC), which is estimated from relative velocity, relative distance, and relative acceleration. This algorithm ensures there is no sudden braking unless risk of collision is high. The algorithm ensures a smooth and controlled stop without causing discomfort to the driver or passengers by taking into account the safety of the vehicle and the comfort of the ride while braking. The system considerably increases the vehicle’s safety and riding comfort, according to results. To completely evaluate its efficacy and dependability, additional testing and validation in actual situations are necessary. The Automatic Dynamic Braking System (ADBS) represents a promising solution to improve vehicle safety and could have a significant impact on reducing the number of road accidents and fatalities caused by human error.

articleTitle: 360-Degree Signal Coverage: Design and Testing of an Omnidirectional Biquad Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication, and evaluation of an Omnidirectional Biquad Antenna, a critical advancement in wireless communication technology. The antenna offers uniform signal coverage across a 360-degree horizontal plane, making it ideal for applications such as Wi-Fi, IoT, and mobile networks. The study emphasizes the use of a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) to optimize the antenna’s performance, focusing on key parameters like impedance matching, gain, and bandwidth. Empirical results demonstrate that the practical model outperforms traditional dipole antennas and models based on existing research, highlighting the antenna’s potential in next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: A Simulation Analysis of 300 kV DC Power Supply for Neutral Beam Injector Accelerator Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The acceleration grid power supply (AGPS) is an integral part of the neutral beam injector (NBI) system. With the advent of negative-ion based NBIs, output voltage of AGPS is becoming higher and higher, even reaching to 1000 kV as in the case of the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER). The key features that characterizes the AGPS are the low output voltage ripple and fast dynamic response. A rectifier-inverter type system is most suited for the AGPS, as the output voltage can be easily regulated from the inverters which are located at the low voltage side. This also facilitates rapid cutoff of the high voltage output during grid breakdown phenomenon. This paper describes a simulation study of 300 kV, 2.0 A AGPS for powering the prototype NBI being developed at IPR. The power supply comprises of three stages, where each stage has an inverter-coupled step-up transformer-rectifier system having an output voltage of 100 kV. Firstly, design of major components of the power converters were investigated. Next, simulation of the entire power supply was carried out in PSIM software. In the simulation model the thyristorized rectifier and the inverters are controlled by a PI master controller, which ensures the desired performance of the system. The simulation results presents the steady state and dynamic response of the controller to meet the technical requirements of the power supply. Apart from the controller performance, voltage stresses in the transformer winding were also estimated.

articleTitle: AutoDim: Automatic High/Low Beam Transition System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The glare from oncoming vehicles is the major cause for accidents at night time due to impaired visibility. This work showcases an automatic high to low beam transition system that can switch the state of headlights in response to the oncoming traffic. The system is comprised of a raspberry pi zero W which uses an image recognition program to detect the intensity of light that it receives. In case of detection, the system automatically switches to low beam setting using the relays connected to headlight. This plug-and-play kit can be installed in any car or bike, offering a practical solution to prevent further nighttime accidents.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach for Evaluating Fairness in LLMs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are prone to bias that can be introduced in the dataset itself or in the training phase. This can make their output lacking in fairness and hinder certain discriminated groups on the basis of stereotypes that the LLM may have been fed with or learnt. In today’s day and age, LLMs are used to make major decisions and thus it is crucial to identify and remove such bias. In this paper, we have focused on identifying the bias present in medium-sized LLMs such as BERT, RoBERTA, DeBERTa and GPT-1 using bias evaluation metrics such as intrinsic and extrinsic. Both the metrics have been used and bias has been identified in the datasets that the LLMs are being trained on (intrinsic bias) as well as in the outputs of the LLMs for certain queries (extrinsic bias).

articleTitle: AutoCAS: An Automated Classroom Attendance System using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Marking attendance during classes using traditional methods is a tedious and error-prone process. This conventional approach wastes valuable teaching time and can cause errors that affect student records. To address these challenges, we propose an automated attendance system with advanced facial recognition and detection techniques to streamline the process. Our system uses DeepFace for both face detection and recognition, selected after careful comparison with methods such as Haar cascades and YOLOv9. Among the approaches tested, DeepFace demonstrated the highest reliability and precision, effectively identifying students from a single snapshot of the classroom. This automated solution reduces the time and manual effort involved in attendance, making the process more efficient and less intrusive. Our system offers a reliable and user-friendly solution for educators, improving routine classroom operations with minimal disruption.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Hardware Design to Prevent Unauthorized Charging of Electric Vehicle Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Electric vehicles significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions and carbon pollution. They rely on rechargeable batteries, with Lithium-Ion being the most efficient due to their low self-discharge rate, large operating range, high energy density, and long life cycle. This paper introduces an Arduino-based, low-cost hardware system to prevent battery theft in electric vehicles. Vehicle component theft, especially batteries, is a growing problem as they are easy to steal and resell. The prototype presented ensures that a stolen battery is unusable without the owner’s consent. The system uses Arduino and Bluetooth modules to provide a cost-effective solution for vehicle owners. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s ability to effectively prevent unauthorized charging across various scenarios. The system successfully ensures that only authenticated users can charge the battery, offering enhanced security and reliability. These results validate the practicality and robustness of the proposed solution..

articleTitle: Enhancement of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drive-Based Solar-Powered Electric Vehicle Drivetrain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The rising demand for sustainable transportation has sparked significant interest in solar-powered electric vehicles (EVs). However, integrating solar energy into EV drivetrains, particularly those using Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs), presents challenges due to the occasional nature of solar power needed for consistent vehicle performance under varying environmental conditions. This paper introduces a high-performance solar-fed PMSM system for electric vehicles, incorporating advanced control techniques and an intelligent energy management strategy (EMS). The system employs Field-Oriented Control (FOC) for precise motor speed regulation and a Fuzzy Logic-based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm to optimize solar energy harvesting. A lithium-ion battery serves for efficient energy storage, enabling the system to store and use solar power effectively. The EMS dynamically allocates energy between the solar panels, battery, and motor, maximizing energy efficiency and extending the vehicle's range. The system was tested in MATLAB/Simulink simulations and validated using dSPACE DS1104 hardware for real-time control. The simulation results, coupled with hardware testing, demonstrate improved energy efficiency and reduced reliance on external charging sources. These findings position solar-powered EVs as a competitive and sustainable solution for the future, offering significant benefits to industries in EV manufacturing and renewable energy. The integration of solar power not only enhances sustainability but also addresses the growing demand for green and efficient transportation.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of a Solar-Wind Hybrid system for a Residence
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The equatorial regions of the Earth are swathed with sunlight and wind as enormous and renewable energy resources. India, being one of the most densely populated countries with high and increasing energy demand, will gain significantly from renewable energy solutions. This paper will propose a solar-wind hybrid system optimized for the residential energy demands with optimized use of rooftop space, supported by a battery backup for a reliable and uninterrupted power supply. In this system design, the mathematical model developed in HOMER Pro has simulated the combined power generation from solar panels and wind turbines for residential loads. The hybrid system uses VAWTs that have been chosen based on the minimum required maintenance, quiet operation and functionality under different wind directions, and relatively low speeds. They are ideal for installation in rooftops of areas found in urban regions. With reduced reliance on the grid, the hybrid system is improving energy resilience for home users while reducing its ecological impact by lowering greenhouse gases emitted. This integration of solar and wind energy hence comes with a sustainable self-sufficient energy solution making the hybrid systems an important element of the transition toward decentralized and cleaner energy resources to residential applications.

articleTitle: Chaotic Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization and Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithm for Robust Feature Selection in IoT Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The exponential growth of IoT data necessitates efficient feature selection for managing high-dimensional datasets while ensuring optimal classification performance. Traditional algorithms face premature convergence, local optima stagnation, and computational inefficiency. To address these, we used the following three advanced techniques. Chaotic Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (CAPSO) which integrates chaotic maps to improve exploration and diversity, avoiding premature convergence. It achieves 40%-60% feature reduction, 97%-98% accuracy, and 2%-3% higher accuracy scores than standard PSO. Hybrid Quantum Genetic Algorithm (HQGA) employs quantum principles to escape local optima, achieving 50%-65% feature reduction, 2% higher accuracy than CAPSO, and 10%-15% lower computational cost. Deep Learning-Assisted Chaotic Sparrow Search Algorithm (DLCSSA) combines chaotic maps with SSA and deep learning (e.g., transformer-based models) to guide the fitness function. It achieves 45%-55% feature reduction, 98%-99% accuracy, and 20% computational savings compared to standard SSA. By integrating chaos theory, quantum mechanics, and deep learning, these state-of-the-art methods significantly enhance performance, reduce computational costs, and improve robustness in IoT data analytics.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Control Protocol for on Board System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The Control Area Network (CAN) protocol is a powerful data bus standard designed to facilitate communication between multiple microcontrollers in a vehicle. industrial automation systems without requiring a host computer. Developed by Bosch in 1983, CAN has become a standard in the automotive industry due to its reliability and efficiency in handling real-time data transmission. CAN operates on a multi-master, message-oriented architecture. It utilizes differential signaling to provide high noise immunity and error detection capabilities, ensuring reliable data communication even in harsh environments. The protocol supports various frame formats, including standard (11-bit identifier) and extended (29-bit identifier) frames, allowing for a wide range of applications. One of the key features of CAN is its arbitration process, which prioritizes messages based on their identifiers. This enables high-priority messages to access the bus first, ensuring timely and critical data transmission. Additionally, CAN FD (Flexible Data Rate) and CAN XL (extended data Length) have been introduced to enhance data throughput and accommodate larger payloads, addressing the growing data demands in modern vehicles. CAN is widely used in electric vehicles (EVs) to enable seamless communication between different electronic control units (ECUs), such as battery management systems, motor controllers, and safety systems. Its efficiency, reliability, and flexibility make it an integral part of the electronic communication architecture in EVs and various other applications, in this paper we are also used the varies type of protocol which is used in Electrical vehicle communication.

articleTitle: Second-Order Consensus in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems by Distributed Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper investigates second-order consensus in heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMASs) using a distributed sliding mode control (DSMC) strategy. The considered system operates with agents having diverse dynamic characteristics, including linear and nonlinear dynamics. A distributed control law is designed to ensure consensus among all agents, facilitating synchronization of their positions and velocities. The proposed control approach leverages sliding mode control to achieve finite-time convergence of consensus errors while ensuring robustness against system heterogeneity. Lyapunov-based stability analysis confirms the theoretical convergence of the system. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the control scheme in achieving second-order consensus in heterogeneous agent networks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Frequency Regulation under a Deregulated Control System Using Distributed Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Now a day, electrical vehicles and their linked control framework are the key points for the power system and its framework. Even design and implementation for an electrical vehicle (EV) with programmed era control under a linked control framework. Both stated requirements are fulfilled here with a representation of result validations. This editorial presents two areas thermal-thermal non-reheat frameworks that are studied in a deregulated environment. Distinctive case studies of the first as a two-sided/bilateral contract and the second as a contract violation with EV behaviour have been produced and exhibited using the DISCO interest framework. The prevalence of lattice-associated Conveyed Vitality Capacity (EVs) has been demonstrated by a comparison of movements with and without EVs to dampen recurrence. Furthermore, the reasonable outcomes for the fuzzy-tuned PI controller & the simple PI controller were assessed. The advantages of minimizing fluctuation time and peak overshoots are discussed and demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Global Challenge, A Global Solution: Battery Reuse and Recycling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries have become integral to modern technology, powering a wide range of devices from smartphones to electric vehicles. As the demand for these batteries continues to grow, the need for sustainable solutions to their disposal and recycling has become increasingly pressing. This research paper explores the current state of lithium-ion battery recycling, the challenges and opportunities it presents, and the potential impact of sustainable recycling technologies on the overall environment’ overall environmental and economic sustainability. The rapid adoption of battery electric vehicles has driven the growing global demand for lithium-ion batteries. This widespread adoption of electric vehicles, coupled with the increasing reliance on portable electronic devices, has fueled the expansion of the lithium-ion battery market.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking Using Particle Swarm Optimization for Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The particle swarm optimization (PSO) technique for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in solar photovoltaic (PV) system under several environmental circumstances is investigated in this work. Four cases are examined: (i) constant irradiation and temperature, (ii) partial shading with constant temperature, (iii) constant irradiation with varying temperature, and (iv) partial shading with varying temperature. PSO optimized power extraction in all cases, effectively tracking the global Maximum Power Point (GMPP) and avoiding local maxima in partial shading. The algorithm adapted well to irradiance and temperature changes, enhancing PV system efficiency. The results obtained from PSO are compared with Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA), showing superior performance. PSO demonstrates better convergence time and tracking efficiency compared to FPA. These findings suggest that PSO can significantly improve performance in large-scale PV installations exposed to environmental challenges like shading and temperature variations.

articleTitle: Commercial and Technological Feasibility of Solar Powered e-Rickshaw: A Case Study in the Capital of Chhattisgarh
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: India accounts for around $18 \%$ of global CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions from transportation. Transportation with conventional energy sources such as coal, oil, and natural gas is costly and poses environmental challenges. The Government of India promotes and subsidizes electric vehicles for fast adoption. The e-Rickshaw is an ideal option for short-distance travel in urban areas due to its low cost. However, one major challenge of e-Rickshaws is battery charging for long-distance travel. In this research article, a survey of e-Rickshaws is conducted in the capital of Chhattisgarh, with an e-Rickshaw powered by a flexible solar photovoltaic (PV) module ($\mathbf{4 2 5} \mathbf{~ W p}$) with a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) charge controller, properly designed, installed, and commissioned on the roof of the vehicle. A comparative analysis of a conventional e-Rickshaw and an e-Rickshaw integrated with a solar PV module is presented. The conventional e-Rickshaw consumes around 7-9 units of electricity per day to fully charge the batteries, resulting in an annual utility bill of approximately Rs. $15,330-19,710$ at a rate of Rs. 6.0 per unit. After integrating the PV module, the e-Rickshaw operator can save up to Rs. 5,475 per year. Additionally, the operator’s travel range and income increase by up to Rs. 7,200 per month. Solar PV integration on the e-Rickshaw mitigates about 0.56 tonnes of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions per year per e-Rickshaw.

articleTitle: Optimizing Grid Resilience and Sustainability with Renewable Energy and Battery Energy Storage Systems.
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The global energy landscape is undergoing a significant transformation, driven by increasing concerns over climate change and the depletion of fossil fuel resources. The integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, into the existing grid offers a promising solution to address these challenges. However, the intermittent nature of these sources poses significant challenges to grid stability and reliability. Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) can mitigate these issues by storing excess energy during periods of high generation and releasing it during periods of low generation or high demand. This paper explores the potential of integrating solar, wind, and BESS technologies into the existing grid to enhance its resilience and sustainability. By optimizing the deployment and operation of these technologies, we can significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate the impacts of climate change. The paper will delve into various aspects, including power conditioning models for the Solar PV subsystem, Wind subsystem, and BESS, with Electric Vehicle (EV) as load connected to the grid. The model is designed and simulated in MATLAB Simulink and focuses on creating a sustainable grid to power electric vehicles. Simulation results demonstrate that the integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and BESS significantly enhances grid resilience and sustainability. The system effectively maintains a constant 48 V DC link voltage under various operating conditions, including fluctuating renewable energy generation and varying EV charging demands, ensuring reliable power delivery to the grid. By effectively leveraging renewable energy and BESS technologies, we can build a more sustainable, resilient, and environmentally friendly energy future.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Dielectric Properties of ZnO and NiO Nanoparticles for Energy Storage Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Nickel oxide (NiO) and zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles were synthesized via an eco-friendly solution-combustion method utilizing lemon juice as a biofuel. Structural, morphological, and dielectric properties were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and dielectric spectroscopy. Rietveld refinement of XRD data confirmed the nanocrystalline nature of both materials, with NiO exhibiting a face-centered cubic structure and ZnO adopting a hexagonal wurtzite configuration. SEM images revealed agglomerated particles with irregular morphology. Dielectric studies conducted over a frequency range of 50 Hz–1 MHz and temperatures of 30– 250 °C demonstrated that NiO possesses a significantly higher dielectric constant (12,000 at 50 Hz, 30 °C) compared to ZnO (480 at 50 Hz, 250 °C). While NiO showed superior energy storage potential, its higher dielectric loss indicates greater energy dissipation. Impedance and AC conductivity analyses highlighted temperature- and frequency-dependent behaviors, underscoring the suitability of these materials for energy-efficient devices.

articleTitle: Markov Modelling of Sustainable Electric Vehicle Infrastructures Using Priority Queues
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Managing the fast charging facilities on green highway networks remains a challenge, and it is not unusual that the rapidly growing electric vehicle (EV) sector has made the availability of charging infrastructure an essential requirement for green and sustainable transportation. This study offers a new approach that provides an analytical framework and performance evaluation for a non-preemptive priority-based queuing model under a general EV charging infrastructure with varying service rates and arrival patterns per priority classification. A new strategy for EV infrastructure sustainability through resource allocation is addressed by the mathematical framework based on Markov chains since it has certain features. Performance metrics based on priority queues, waiting times, service demand, and the overall system performance are utilized to validate our model. The proposed approach assists in managing EV charging stations and has the simultaneous advantages of fostering widespread adoption of environmentally friendly methods of transport without negatively impacting customer satisfaction and ensuring high operational effectiveness.

articleTitle: Enhanced Two-Degree-of-Freedom Control for Polynomial and Sinewave Reference Trajectories
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Most of the control system design requires output signal to follow setpoint trajectories with zero steady state error. A discrete-time PID controller often struggles to track complex reference trajectories like sinusoidal and ramp signals, resulting in steady-state errors. However, real-time tuning of a PID controller can be quite challenging, and it also tends to lack the ability to reject disturbances effectively. A two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) controller structure offers a solution by enabling improved tracking performance of such reference trajectories. While recent approaches have successfully addressed steady-state error removal for polynomial trajectories, this paper extends these methods to sinusoidal reference signals. Additionally, it explores a combined approach for tracking both sinusoidal and polynomial references by leveraging the Auxiliary Aryabhatta’s Identity Equation. The control strategy has been validated on a thermal resistive plant utilizing both cyclic and ramping temperature setpoint profiles.

articleTitle: Solar Powered EV Charging Station with Improved Adaptive LMS Control for V2G and G2V Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: A sustainable and effective charging infrastructure is essential to using electric vehicles (EVs). The challenges of developing a sustainable and efficient EV charging infrastructure are addressed in this study by offering a novel solution: a solar PV-based charging system combined with a Zero Attracting Improved Proportionate Normalised Least Mean Square (IZA-PNLMS) adaptive control algorithm IZA-PNLMS performs better than the existing method in minimizing harmonic distortion, preserving voltage stability, and enabling optimal power extraction from solar panels, efficient EV charging, and smooth grid integration due to its faster convergence, lower error, and DC offset rejection. This article discusses the proposed technology, implementation, and performance evaluation in depth to achieve grid compliance, improved power quality, and sustained and effective EV charging. By examining simulation results under several transient modes, the proper V2G and G2V methods are confirmed.

Author Keywords: Improved Zero Attracting Proportionate Normalized Least Mean Square (IZA-PNLMS)

articleTitle: Flexible Operation of Combined cycle Gas Based Power Plants in Western Region, India
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Indian Power Sector is continuously evolving with the integration of significant renewable capacity i.e. 500GW by 2030 [1]. To integrate the substantial renewable generation capacity into the grid, flexible generation resources need to be harnessed to the extent possible for which several measures are being implemented in India i.e. reducing the minimum turndown level of thermal plants to 40% from 55%, rejuvenating existing imported coal and gas-based power plants. Efforts are also made to increase the penetration of hydroelectric, pumped storage plants and battery energy storage systems in the Indian energy mix. This paper examines the operational practices of gas based power plants in Western Region of India, analyzing historical data to identify opportunities for enhanced flexibility. By exploring the current operational practices, the paper aims to unlock the full flexibility potential, enabling gas based plants to effectively support the integration of renewable energy sources.

Author Keywords: Closed Cycle Operation of Gas Turbines

articleTitle: Comparative performance analysis of AOA-SHE control for SC-MLI with SO-SHE and PSO-SHE based control scheme
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are widely acknowledged as dependable power converters for photovoltaic (PV) applications, producing AC across the load from DC sources. Among the numerous MLI types, switched-capacitor MLIs (SC-MLIs) are gaining popularity for production of enhanced output with one step conversion. Current research focuses on reducing the number of circuit elements, lowering total harmonic distortion (THD), and controlling voltage stress on switches in SC-MLIs. This has resulted in the creation of new inverter topologies with effective control techniques. In this respect, this paper offers a new boost-type SC-MLI design that incorporates an Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (AOA)-based Selective Harmonic Elimination (SHE) control method for standalone PV systems. The model is tested under a variety of situations in the MATLAB/Simulink environment to illustrate the feasibility of the proposed a new SC-MLI that contain one source with low stress on switches, low-cost factor with AOA-based SHE control. It is also contrasted to the recently implemented SO-based SHE control and conventional Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-based SHE control approaches to evaluate the AOA-SHE control method's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Comparative Assessment of MPPT Techniques for Optimizing Photovoltaic System Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The weather uncertainties and fluctuating nature of solar radiations and varying temperature results in low conversion efficiency of the PV panel thereby necessitating the extraction of maximum power from the system. To operate the system at its peak power, track of maximum power point becomes essential for any PV system. To handle the input fluctuations and inherent non-linearities of the system, an effective MPPT technique needs to be employed. In this research paper, various classical and intelligent MPPT techniques are listed, discussed and compared on various parameters. The classical Incremental Conductance algorithm, intelligent MPPT based on fuzzy logic control and ANN method is designed and tested on a PV system using MATLAB/Simulink. The PV system entails a PV array, a boost converter, MPPT control unit, and load. These methods diverge in their characteristics and their performance is evaluated on various parameters such as tracking efficiency, response time, implementation complexity, and stability under dynamic conditions. In this work, the drawbacks of the studied methods are also pointed out. Among the implemented techniques, superiority of neural network based MPPT technique is established over the classical as well Fuzzy Logic based MPPT controller for optimizing the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Differential Protection of Electrical Busbar considering CT Saturation Detection using Power Spectral Density
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Implementing proper busbar protection techniques is crucial for ensuring the security and reliability of electrical power distribution systems. By employing appropriate protection schemes, such as differential and overcurrent protection, busbar can be safeguarded from various faults, including short circuits and abnormal operating conditions. This is essential for preventing damage to the system and ensuring uninterrupted power supply to critical loads. An innovative method for busbar differential protection has been proposed, utilizing spectral power density as a key parameter. This innovative method aims to enhance the sensitivity of fault detection by adaptively changing the slope of the differential relay while also improving the system’s ability to differentiate between various faults and abnormal conditions. This advancement holds the potential to significantly improve the reliability and effectiveness of busbar protection systems in power distribution networks. This technique is immune to various levels of degree of CT saturation, hence making the system more reliable and stable in case of an internal/external fault occurrence. The model has been simulated on PSCAD and the results are verified giving better performance as compared to the conventional differential protection method.

articleTitle: Time-Series Forecasting of Energy Consumption Using LSTM Networks for Optimized Microgrid Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Accurate energy consumption forecasting is crucial for the efficient management of microgrids, especially as renewable energy sources become increasingly integrated into power systems. In this paper, we present a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) based model for time-series forecasting of energy consumption using smart meter data from Bareilly, India. The dataset, consisting of over six million samples recorded at threeminute intervals, was preprocessed and used to train an LSTM network that effectively captures temporal dependencies in energy usage. The model was evaluated using metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ score, demonstrating its strong predictive performance with an $R^{2}$ value of 0.85984. While the model accurately predicts most energy usage patterns, it faces challenges in capturing extreme consumption spikes. These results highlight the potential of deep learning models in optimizing energy distribution.

articleTitle: Harmonic Mitigation Using Active and Passive Filters
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: With the growing trend in usage of electric vehicles (EVs), potential harmonic distortion that could be caused by nonlinear EV battery charging are being looked at closely as they would affect operation and functionality of the power grid. In this study, the implication of active and passive filter for harmonic distortion reduction, in EV battery charging system is presented. Active filters using real-time power electronics and control algorithms achieve up to $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$ THD suppression, whereas passive filters provide a low-cost option with up to $85 \%$ reduction in THD. The results show that both types of filters are effective in enhancing the power quality. This work offers practical guidelines on filter design, optimization, and performance assessment to enable effective and green EV charging infrastructure

articleTitle: Enhanced Automated Brain Tumour Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Precise identification of brain tumors is important for treatment and outcomes. Manual analysis of MRI scans is very time-consuming and prone to errors. This paper explores the application of CNNs for automatic classification of brain MRI scans to help radiologists provide rapid and accurate diagnoses. The dataset was pre-processed to ensure consistency and generalizability through resizing, normalization, and data augmentation. Data augmentation methods include rotating, flipping, and brightening have been applied to deal with few numbers of training images, enhancing the model. Convolutional, pooling, and dropout layers in the CNN architecture are focused to achieve feature extraction, avoid overfitting, and recognize brain tumors. It has also been optimized using Adam with its testing process concerning accuracy, precision, and recall. Excellent generalization of $\mathbf{9 4 \%}$ training and $\mathbf{9 1 \%}$ validation. Good scores for the cases producing high precision and high recall validate the correctness in no false positives as well as false negatives of tumor detection by this model. Results improve efficiency and accuracy of the diagnostic process, aiding timeand consistency-strained radiologists. Larger sets and architecture refinement as future works could make it more relevantly clinically for testing across various settings.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Cuckoo Search MPPT Algorithm for Solar Photovoltaic Inverter Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: As the demand for renewable energy sources continues to grow, optimizing the efficiency of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems becomes increasingly important. This study illustrates a solar PV system that determines maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in solar inverter applications adopting a Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA). The CSA provides a distinctive approach for determining the maximum power under various scenarios and is modeled after the brood parasitism of some cuckoo species. This study examines the algorithm’s performance in real-time tracking of maximum power output, analyzing its responsiveness to change in irradiance and temperature. Simulation results using MATLAB demonstrate that the CSA achieves greater efficiency and faster convergence compared to traditional MPPT methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Differential Protection of Large-Scale Generator Considering CT Saturation Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Synchronous generators are the most complex machines in the power plant requiring protection against constant and transient stresses for reliable operation of the power system. A differential protection scheme and a current transformer (CT) are provided to protect the stator from internal faults. CT saturation in the event of external disturbances may influence relay operation which is not intended. The standard differential protection of synchronous generator lags to distinguish between faults internal and external to the stator which may lead to false tripping of the relay causing disturbances in the power system. This requires modification in relay characteristics to provide adaptive operation. This paper proposes an adaptive differential protection technique with increased sensitivity using DFT for stator protection of a large-scale 3-phase synchronous generator from internal faults considering various levels of CT saturation. The simulation of synchronous generator is done using PSCAD software. To study the impact of CT saturation under conditions of internal fault and external fault various situations were intentionally developed. The basis of discrimination is the slope of flux density with respect to time in the core of CT. System outcomes of simulations for such situations were obtained. The results demonstrate the potency of the suggested relaying technique in discriminating between faults internal and external to the stator of the synchronous generator.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Energy Efficiency of a custom developed Physically Unclonable Function(PUF) for IoT Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) has gathered attention from academia and industry as a possible substitute for the more typical computational-based method of applying conventional encryption to protect Internet of Things (IoT) devices. With its minimal design complexity and confidentiality preservation, PUF is a potential lightweight security solution that uses the IC manufacturing fluctuation process to enhance IoT security. We used a custom-designed PUF system which offers lower computing resources and costs, compared to other PUF systems. This PUF system is helpful develop a low-cost device for IoT security.

articleTitle: A Review Summary on Recent Trends in Application of Li-ion Battery in Power Delivery System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Electrical energy generation by conventional methods, their transportation to the load end, and the distribution among the electric consumers becomes complex day by day due to unscheduled insertion of generated power by distributed energy resources (DER). As most of the distributed generations are integrated into the distributed system (DS), the variability in power generation and consumption increases, and the DS operation becomes more vulnerable. The generation and injection of electricity from DER during the peak generation to the DS may not match the peak demand hours, which is a big challenge for the distribution operator in managing the power. Due to uncertain availability and power injection, the power purchased from the grid by the utility becomes irregular and adversely affects the DS economy. To address the said problem a detailed survey has been performed in this paper and the research opportunities are demonstrated considering the minimization of different attributes like SADPL, SADD, and SAENS by the optimal operation of the electric energy storage system like Li-ion BES. This study can lend a helping hand to researchers to investigate the electrical power distribution system’s (PDS) techno-economic performance improvement with a reliable power supply, which could be a win-win solution for both utility and needy electric consumers.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Hydrogen Storage: Addressing Geo-storage and Critical Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This study assesses the potential of underground hydrogen storage in porous rock formations found in depleted oil/gas fields, saline aquifers, solution-mined salt caverns, and engineered rock caverns. The task is to enhance the quantity of hydrogen stored on the surface while ensuring the safe and long-term subsurface storage of hydrogen in compatible reservoir formations, eliminating any potential leakage. Hydrogen Geo-storage (HGS) is a process of injecting and storing hydrogen into subsurface formation, which is a significantly longer-term perspective underground storage of Hydrogen. It is an effort to achieve net-zero decarburization for future climate change mitigation and reduce the footprint of greenhouse gases. The paper outlines the need for underground gas storage, explores the technical aspects of hydrogen gas storage, and evaluates the geological, environmental, and storage media criteria. It addresses challenges such as the risks of hydrogen conversion, loss, leakage and contamination from microbial activity, discusses the role of cushion gas, reviews legal and regulatory conditions, and concludes with recommendations for the safe and effective adoption of HGS. The objective is to understand solid-fluid and fluid-fluid interactions within storage formations to optimize HGS processes while ensuring safe and environmentally friendly reservoir performance. A comprehensive consideration of technical, environmental, and legal aspects is essential for successful hydrogen geo storage.

articleTitle: Analytical study for detecting rusting in cylindrical pillars in L Band
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of electromagnetic scattering in finding rust in reinforced cement concrete structures in non-destructive way. The analytical analysis shown here employs Maxwell’s equations and applies suitable boundary conditions to solve the three-layer cylinder at varying levels of rusting. The scattered and total electric fields at 1 GHz for varying rusting levels demonstrate that the rust can be detected in a non-invasive way.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Pruning and Quantization Methods for Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: As deep learning models are increasingly being deployed on resource-constrained edge devices, the need to develop techniques to make the model more energy efficient without sacrificing its performance becomes crucial. In this study we explored the three most prominent approaches, such as bit quantization, model pruning, and adaptive switching techniques to address the computational and memory overheads of deep neural networks. Bit quantization reduces the weight and activation precisions, effectively lowering the hardware requirements for both storage and computation. Again the model pruning eliminates redundant parameters; thus, reduces the model complexity, and boost the inference time. Along with all these methods the adaptive switching techniques allow the model’s parameters or structure to switch at run-time so that trade-off between accuracy and energy consumption is dynamically optimized. In this paper we explored the advantages and limitations of such techniques for edge devices through a comprehensive study of recent advancements and methodologies. Point out that the open challenge on how to balance model performance with energy efficiency and future directions for the optimization of deep learning models for edge computing environments.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Regularization and Mini-Batch Training Techniques for ANN Based Wind Speed Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Wind Speed (WS) prediction is a complex task due to its non-linear and dynamic nature. Machine learning models are commonly used for this purpose therefore prediction accuracy of the models remains a challenging problem now a days. In this study L2, L1 regularization, early stopping and batch normalization are used for comparative analysis in WS prediction. It is evaluated by Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R-squared ($\mathrm{R}^{2}$). For tasks with similar characteristics, prioritize using L1 Regularization as it demonstrates the best balance of error reduction and generalization. Re-evaluate the use of Batch Normalization and Early Stopping for this context, possibly in conjunction with other techniques, to improve their effectiveness.

articleTitle: AntiMicrobial Resistance Prediction Using Advanced Image Encoding Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the significant problems in the health sector and requires resources to create and develop accurate forecasting systems capable of recognizing resistant microbes and their treatment approaches. The traditional machine learning models used in AMR prediction usually suffer from poor genomic sequences feature extraction and finding it hard to solve big biological problems with big data. K-mer based methods or other simpler classifiers have been able to provide certain accuracy, but these have strived when dealing with many genomic strains and variants. To address these shortcomings, deep learning models are able to learn data representation at various abstraction levels which understanding complex data of fundamental and high dimensional patterns. In this work we provide a new deep learning approach exploiting CNNs on FCGR images of microbial genomes. The sequence is represented as frequency chaos game representation making it better for the enn structural application as resnet and densenet where features are deeply embedded in classifiers. When it comes to string and image based methods it is clear that they both have their own benefits and shortcomings. String based analysis is a faster and more accurate way to analyze naked sequence data conversion, but it may not be as informative as visual presentation. Our study verified the hypothesis that it is feasible to encode genomic data for further FCGR, so that the data might be utilized as an input for machine learning and deep learning methods. The model is effective with substantial improvements with the accuracy of over $90 \%$ in test dataset. This represents a significant improvement in accuracy score with better systems for predicting antibiotic resistance among many types of microbes.

articleTitle: Phase Change Materials in Thermal Energy Storage: A Comprehensive Review of Properties, Advances, and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Thermal energy storage (TES) technology relies on phase change materials (PCMs) to provide high-quality, high-energy density heat storage. However, their cost, poor structural performance, and low heat conductivity restrict their practical use. The current status of PCM technology in TES applications is examined in this paper, with a focus on important traits, recent advancements, persistent challenges, and possible future directions. The study covers the basic thermal characteristics of PCMs, including latent heat capacity, specific heat, and thermal conductivity. The advantages and disadvantages of both organic and inorganic PCMs are emphasized. Recent work has focused on composite PCMs, hybrid nanofluidics, and shape stabilized forms to address structural stability and heat transfer efficiency. The paper also discusses knowledge gaps that need to be filled, such as understanding PCM behaviour in real-world conditions and external stimuli. The paper proposes cost-effectiveness and sustainability of PCM-based TES systems for large-scale use in commercial and industrial sectors. The review aims to direct future research directions and foster sustainable, efficient energy storage technologies for contemporary energy management and conservation.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of PV fed Dynamic Voltage Restorer using UVTG and Hysteresis Voltage Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Dynamic voltage Restorer is one of the devices to solve the voltage related power quality issues. Now the recent trends is Photo Voltaic (PV) fed DVR. Research on PV fed DVR in power quality analysis is presented in many papers. In this paper, a PV fed DVR is designed to analyze the voltage related power quality issues such as voltage sag, voltage swell and harmonics in a distribution system. The investigation is mainly focused on the proper implementation of the control algorithm in the proposed DVR and the accurate compensation of voltage in all of the problems, Unit Vector Template Generation (UVTG) Phase Locked Loop (PLL) is suggested in this work to generate the reference signal along with output of Proportional Integral (PI) controller. Hysteresis voltage controller loop is used to generate the switching signal of the voltage source inverter which is the important part of the DVR. PV is used to maintain the DClink voltage as well as maintain the power supply in case of problems in the grid. The work is carried out with MATLAB/SIMULINK platform to verify the effectiveness of the suggested controller

articleTitle: Sustainable Modeling Framework for the Prediction in Ungauged Catchments: Leveraging Large-Sample Hydrology Datasets with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Predicting hydrological behavior in ungauged basins presents a major challenge for sustainable water resource management in regions with limited data, such as the Indian subcontinent. Accurate prediction of water availability typically requires calibrating hydrological models using historical discharge data, which is often unavailable for many Indian catchments. In this context, comparative hydrology remains a valuable approach, as comparing diverse catchments has proven effective in understanding and forecasting hydrological processes, particularly in ungauged regions.This study focuses on the critical role of catchment characteristics in improving the prediction of hydrological responses in ungauged basins across 4 countries. By employing large-sample hydrology methods, we analyze comprehensive datasets from gauged basins worldwide and compare them to Indian ungauged basins to identify patterns that can be applied for predictive purposes. For this analysis, we use the CAMELS (Catchment Attributes and Meteorology for Large-sample Studies) datasets from the USA, Australia, and Chile for physio-climatic data. For India, we compile data from 216 catchments, categorize it into three groups based on attributes, and evaluate clustering using Normalized Mutual Information. We also correlate catchment features-such as soil properties and vegetation cover-with hydrological responses.Our findings demonstrate how attribute-based clustering of catchments can be leveraged to identify similar catchments over large spatial scales. Ungauged basins that share significant similarities with gauged basins can benefit from the extrapolation of data, enabling more accurate predictions. Additionally, incorporating climatic indices with catchment attributes enhances the accuracy of hydrological forecasts under different climate conditions.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multi-phase Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The design, implementation, and performance analysis of a DC-DC multi-phase buck converter (MBC) has been explained, it is a three-phase power supply system. The study highlights the advantages of multi-phase configurations, which utilize parallel-connected buck converter phases sharing input and output capacitors, over conventional single-phase designs.
