The Arduino ATMEGA 2560 generates the programmable gate pulses at a frequency of 10 kHz enhancing control flexibility. The experimental results reveal a significant reduction in output voltage ripple with improved efficiency. The MBC’s capability to minimize capacitor charging and discharging times has been demonstrated successfully. These findings underscore the potential of multi-phase buck converters for high-power applications requiring rapid voltage adjustments and minimal ripple.

articleTitle: AI-Based Trash Collector Boat for Autonomous Waterway Pollution Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This project develops an AI-powered autonomous boat for the collection of waste thrown into rivers, lakes, and coastlines. The “trash boat” will make use of computer vision in order to detect, classify, and collect floating waste, including plastics and other pollutants. Equipped with sensors, cameras, and AI algorithms, the system identifies where the waste is, navigate toward it, collect it, and offers clear avoidance of obstacles to ensure safe and efficient navigation. Aimed is to minimize the various forms of water pollution thereby protect marine ecosystems and support environmental sustainability through continuous autonomous waste collection within unreachable or water areas greatly polluted.

articleTitle: Power Factor Correction(PFC) for EV Charger Using PI Controller in G2V Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents an AC-DC converter system tailored for grid-to-vehicle (G2V) applications, aimed at facilitating efficient power flow while achieving a Unity power factor (UPF). The system employs a rectifier for AC-DC conversion, which effectively steps up a 230V AC input to a 380V DC output. This DC output can be further regulated using a buck converter to meet specific load requirements. A Proportional-Integral (PI) controller is implemented to oversee the voltage and current regulation, thereby minimizing harmonic distortion and enhancing the overall power factor. By actively managing the input voltage and current, the controller ensures that the system operates within desired parameters, thus optimizing power quality. Comprehensive simulation results validate the system’s performance, demonstrating its capability to maintain a UPF in G2V mode. The findings indicate significant reductions in total harmonic distortion (THD), reinforcing the system’s effectiveness in managing power quality. This AC-DC converter design not only enhances the efficiency of power flow in electric vehicle charging systems but also contributes to the stability of the grid by minimizing reactive power and harmonics. Overall, this work represents a significant advancement in converter technology for sustainable transportation and energy management.

articleTitle: Experimental Insights into the Modeling and Control of Heater Systems Using Discrete PID Controllers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This research presents the real-time implementation of discrete PI and PID control algorithms on a Heater System, with the system model identified through open-loop experiments using the Scilab platform. A First-Order Plus Dead Time model is fitted to the experimental data, and controller parameters are determined using the tuning method. The study investigates the impact of disturbances, modeled by a DC fan, on temperature control and compares the performance of different control strategies. The PID and PID with filter controllers show improved disturbance rejection, faster response, and reduced steady-state error, offering valuable insights for selecting the most effective control algorithm for temperature control in such systems.

articleTitle: Reversing Voltage Topology for Multi-Level Inverters: Simulation and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: In recent years, using multi-level inverters for high power, high voltage applications has grown in popularity. Their performance is far better than standard two level inverters in terms of less harmonic distortion, decreased electromagnetic interference, and higher dc link voltages.It might have certain drawbacks, such as a higher component count, a more difficult PWM control scheme, and a floating neutral point. This work introduces a novel architecture called Reversing Voltage (RV) to enhance the multilevel performance and compared it for different levels (up to eleven level) to show reduced % THD in output voltage at higher level. This design uses less carrier signals and switches than standard inverters, especially at higher levels. It also eliminates the need for voltage balancing. Phase disposition SPWM technology is the basis for both the topology and control mechanism. Lastly, comparisons are made between the experimental (Laboratory Proto-type Model for Single Phase Five-Level Inverter Using Reversing Voltage Topology) and simulation findings at various voltage levels. The outcomes of the experiment closely resemble those of the simulation.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Relationship of Carbon Dioxide Level with Physical Parameters in IoT-based Greenhouse Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The study presents a comprehensive solution for monitoring and optimizing environmental conditions within a greenhouse using Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The greenhouse effect is critical for the cultivation of crops, and maintaining optimal parameters such as humidity, temperature, carbon dioxide level, atmospheric pressure is paramount for efficient plant growth. This system employs a network of sensors connected through IoT to collect real-time data. The proposed system comprises a sensor array strategically placed within the greenhouse to continuously measure key environmental parameters. These sensors transmit data wirelessly to a centralized IoT gateway, which processes the information and uploads it to a cloud-based platform for storage and analysis. The collected data is further analyzed and the carbon dioxide print with respect to day-to-day temperature, humidity and atmospheric pressure present inside the greenhouse is determined. This study provided insights into optimizing crop cultivation through CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> level analysis.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Power-Flow Solutions in Radial Distribution Network with 12, 33, and 69 IEEE Bus System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The study involves creating power flow equations, network representation, and iterative methods such as Newton-Raphson and Gauss-Seidel to solve them. However, these traditional methods may not always yield accurate results, particularly for distribution systems. For more precise analysis, the Forward/Backward Sweep algorithm is employed in radial distribution systems (RDS), effectively calculating branch power flows, bus voltages, and system parameters like node voltage, line current, and branch current. This paper explores the application of the Forward/Backward Sweep method for load flow analysis in RDSs, using a 12-bus, 33-bus, and 69-bus system as examples. By determining bus voltages in the forward sweep and branch currents in the backward sweep, the method ensures an accurate evaluation of system performance, including total active and reactive power and power loss. The entire study has been carried out on MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Overcurrent Relays Coordination of Interconnected Power System using Modified Objective Functions and Multiple Standardized Tripping Curves
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Over the last few decades, many researchers opt various techniques to achieve optimum time for coordination of overcurrent relays. The main motive of these techniques is to avoid mal operation among the main and secondary relays and to reduce time of operation of each relay as per required criteria. Some researchers have suggested modification in relay characteristics and objective functions to avoid mis-coordination. Three objective functions from the literature are examined in this paper, and new modified objective functions are the suggested after modification. A comparison is made between the standard objective function with modified obje ctive functions. Out of three modified objective functions, the best modified objective function is proposed. Further, three IEC standard relay characteristics have been adopted to analyze & compare the effectiveness & robustness of said objective functions. For the said comparison IEEE 14-bus modified distribution system is considered and a Harmony search algorithm is used.

articleTitle: Comparitive analysis between coulomb counting algorithm and adaptive kalman filter algorithm for SOC estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: State of Charge (SOC) and State of Health (SOH) are two key parameters in battery performance management, especially for electric vehicle and energy storage applications. Accurate estimation of them is required to ensure the reliability, safety, and efficiency of a battery. This review paper presents various estimation techniques developed for SOC and SOH, including Coulomb counting filters, Adaptive Kalman filters. Each technique is discussed on the basis of strengths and limits, accuracy, computational demand, and suitability for real-time applications. This paper will facilitate selecting the best estimator based on needs and conditions for research and engineers. Discussion on the recent advancement and trend of the estimator technologies is made to reflect upon future research directions.

Author Keywords: Ratio of remaining capacity to the maximum capacity.
Ratio of maximum battery charged now to the fully charged capacity.

articleTitle: IoT based pulse rate monitor powered with energy harvester
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Systems for remotely monitoring patients are useful because they can deliver prompt and efficient medical care. Wearable sensor technologies that are highly developed and precise are typically utilized to facilitate internet telemedicine. Vital sign metrics including pulse rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, respiration rate, and temperature of the body can all be monitored with the current generation of wearable, connected gadgets. The main issue with wearable technology is that it requires a lot of power to transmit signals. This means that regular battery changes are necessary, which severely restricts the ability to continuously monitor important data. In order to get around this, the present research offers a main report on tracking vital human indicators by measuring the kinetic energy of ordinary human activity. The energy that is captured is utilized to keep wearable devices’ batteries charged, extending the time that important data may be monitored. Based on a microcontroller (ATMega328) and a Wi-Fi device (ESP8266), this study suggests a stress- or exercise-monitoring gadget that allows real-time pulse rate monitoring in the cloud during regular daily activities. The harvester has a small, lightweight design. Experiments are conducted to demonstrate the output power generated by the proposed harvester and IoT server is used to show the pulse rate variability of a person in walking scenarios.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Based Solar Power Generation Prediction and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Integration of renewable energy sources with the conventional grid is the key way to sustain the world with the limited conventional sources and also open the door to the green energy system. Solar, wind, hydro and many more are the renewable energy sources connected with the grid; however, its optimization is one of the crucial aspects as the input to these sources is variable and intermittent in nature. This paper deals with the prediction of solar power plant located at Ahmedabad. The simulation work has been carried out with System Advisor Model (SAM) software. Various parameters like temperature, solar irradiance and generated output power have been analysed through this study. Various Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms, Linear regression (LR) model, artificial neural network (ANN) model, support vector machines (SVM) model, random forest (RF) model, gradient boosting (GB) models has been simulated, analysed and compared in results w.r.t the root means square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and correlation coefficient (CC) and fond that for small amount of the power plant data provided here, ANN and SVM fits best as they provide 1 to 10 % error as compared to rest of all errors. CC gives result 1 except SVM algorithm and LR model provides linear relations.

articleTitle: Transformer Oil Analysis using DGA and UV-Visible Spectroscopy for Condition Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Oil-immersed power transformers are critical assets in electrical power system networks from generation to utilization. The insulating oil degrades as it comes under thermal and electrical stress due to continuous operation. This cause’s incipient fault leads to catastrophic transformer failure if precautionary measures are not provided. This paper presents condition monitoring techniques such as Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) and UV-visible spectroscopy. The health status of the transformer is carried out by accurately analyzing the gas contents using DGA technique and at the same time assessment of the oil is carried out using UV-visible spectroscopy by measuring light absorbance at different wavelengths. The combined application of these two techniques facilitates an accurate diagnosis of transformer conditions, enabling effective preventive measures against potential failures.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized High Directivity and Wideband Cruciform Patch Antenna for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper embodies a Cruciform Microstrip patch antenna with a Single layer with a single-patch dual-polarized antenna which provides high gain and directivity along with wide bandwidth. The Proposed antenna design can be useful for base station antennas. The manuscripts present three antenna structures as a process for the development of the final proposed antenna. The proposed antenna is a dual-fed-symmetric antenna, in which the center part is etched out to achieve the properties required for a base station antenna. Along with better gain and bandwidth, the proposed antenna exhibits very good isolation between the two ports with an efficiency of $\mathbf{9 7 \%}$. The proposed antenna is simulated with CST MWS. The proposed antenna has a directivity of about 12.33 dBi, and a bandwidth of 358 MHz, which spans from 4.9 GHz to 5.2 GHz. Two resonating points are evident from the simulation as 4.99 GHz with a return loss of 20.5 dB and 5.22 GHz with a return loss of 16.16 dB.

articleTitle: Structural, Morphological and Dielectric Properties of Green Synthesised TiO2 Nanoparticles for Energy Storage Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Titanium dioxide $\left(\mathrm{TiO}_{2}\right)$ nanoparticles are synthesized by green synthesis method using lemon juice as a fuel. The study aimed to address gaps in the exploration of dielectric properties of green-synthesized $\mathbf{T i O}_{2}$ nanoparticles. The prepared nanoparticles were subjected to different characterizations to understand their structural, morphological and electrical properties. X-ray diffraction (XRD) was used to analyze the structural and phase composition of the produced TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, while energy-dispersive X ray spectroscopy (EDX) was used to know the elemental composition and purity of sample, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) looks at the surface shape and texture and produces comprehensive images of the nanoparticle surfaces. The dielectric properties of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles such as dielectric constant, dielectric loss, impedance, and electric modulus are thoroughly studied as a function of frequency. The material’s dielectric characteristics is seen to be frequency-dependent, according to the study. The obtained results exhibit that prepared material can be used as promising anode material in batteries and super capacitor applications.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Framework for Drought Modeling using Meteorological Drought Indicators as Proxies for Hydrological Drought
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Droughts are among the most severe natural disasters, with profound impacts on human livelihoods, agricultural productivity, and economic stability. Addressing freshwater scarcity through sustainable water resource management remains a global priority, yet accurate estimation of freshwater availability is often hindered by uncertainties in climate projections. In India, this challenge is amplified by the scarcity of streamflow data and the limited availability of reliable hydrological records across catchments. Despite these constraints, the abundance of meteorological data offers an alternative avenue to assess drought conditions. Emerging studies highlight a strong link between meteorological and hydrological droughts, suggesting that meteorological indicators can serve as a proxy to predict hydrological drought dynamics. This study develops a generalized framework to explore the relationship between meteorological and hydrological droughts using twelve diverse catchments across India. The monthly stream flow data were analyzed to calculate the Standardized Streamflow Index (SSI), quantifying the severity of the hydrological drought. Simultaneously, key meteorological drought indices—Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI)—were derived using precipitation and temperature records. Correlation and time-series analyses revealed that meteorological drought indices, combined with catchment-specific characteristics such as soil type, elevation, and topography, can effectively predict hydrological drought conditions in regions with sparse hydrological data. This research enhances our understanding of drought propagation mechanisms in India and provides a foundation for developing early warning systems and informed sustainable water resource management strategies, particularly in data-scarce regions.

articleTitle: Performance of Stacked LSTM for Solar Energy Revenue Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This study investigates the performance of stacked and simplified Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for predicting daily revenue from a 1 MW solar power plant at Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU), Gujarat, India. Utilizing the meteorological and operational data, the models were evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE). The stacked LSTM demonstrated enhanced accuracy, capturing complex temporal dependencies more effectively than the simplified model. The findings highlight the potential of stacked LSTM for improving financial planning and operational efficiency in forecasting different attributes of solar energy generation.

articleTitle: DNN-Driven Voltage Regulation in Wind Energy Systems with Electric Spring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: An Electric Spring (ES) based wind energy system is proposed in this paper for robust voltage management using a Deep Neural Network (DNN). In this research we look at the outline and implementation of a DNN that controls the ES in a wind energy system with difficult loading conditions. Although Electric spring is used for voltage control before, the main improvement is the robustness that the well-trained DNN brings. To train the DNN parameters, a typical distribution network was used to generate the dataset. The learned model was then evaluated on unseen scenarios. By using fewer sensors and being less reliant on grid variables, the results shows that the DNN-driven ES performs better than previous ES implementations.

articleTitle: A Simple Analytical Approach based Model Based Multi-loop PID Controller Design for Typical TITO Distillation Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: In this paper a model-based decentralized PID controller is proposed based on a unified analytical solution. Basically, this proposed approach provides a method that offers an appropriate trade-off between good servo and regulatory response, as well as robustness under parametric perturbation. In this work, to implement the controller, a decoupler is first developed using the dynamics of the binary distillation column model. Then, a reduced-order model is acquired for the decoupled system. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed model-based algorithm two distinct typical case studies have been considered. From the obtained simulation results it is clearly observed that the proposed controller delivers good control action in order to control the binary distillation process

articleTitle: Power Quality Analysis of a Distribution System Using A Novel Shunt Hybrid Filter
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: In this paper, power quality analysis of a distribution system is analyzed with a novel Shunt Hybrid Filter (SHF). The proposed hybrid filter is the combination of a Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) and a Double Tuned Passive Filter (DTPF). The SAPF and DTPF are designed to eliminate lower and the higher order harmonics respectively which are originated due to the nonlinear load in the distribution system. Cascaded DQ theory (Synchronous Reference Frame Technique) and PQ theory (Instantaneous Reactive Power Theory) including Adaptive-Neuro-Fuzzy-Inference System (ANFIS) is proposed as suitable combined controller for SAPF of the proposed SHF. The main objective of this controller is to generate the accurate reference signal for SAPF to obtain the pulse for the converter by comparing it with the original signal. At the same time DTPF undergoes resonance and provides lowest impedance to the particular frequency of the higher order harmonics. The effectiveness of the proposed HAF with the combined controller is verified through MATLAB/SIMULINK platform.

articleTitle: An Inverter Control Strategy Pertaining to PSO Technique in the Grid Connected System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a three phase inverter that is coupled to a grid for photovoltaic operations which features a three phase inverter ans a DC-DC boost converter. To build up the low voltage Direct Current output of a PV configuration to a high voltage Direct Current level for inverter connected to grid, a DC DC boost converter is applied. To switch over Direct Current output of boost converter into a 3 phase Alternate Current output, a three phase grid-connected inverter is applied. This AC output is coherent with the grid voltage. Compared to traditional systems, this system has several advantages. The DC-DC boost converter enables for MPP of a PV array. DC-DC boost converter has low operating duty cycle and the inverter topology presented provides greater efficiency. PI controller is used to control the Id value so as to match with Idref and Iq to match with Iqref which ia equal to zero. PSO algorithm is used for mppt and also as an optimization technique for the controller. The simulation of this topology with MATLAB/SIMULINK revealed the system’s ability to provide superior quality three-phase AC output with lower harmonic distortion.

articleTitle: Antenna Design with high Gain and Efficiency for Millimeter wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The paper presents an compact mmwave microstrip patch antenna operating at 39 GHz suitable for 5 G communications. The radiating patch of the antenna is made with loading a H-Slot and inverted T-Slot on a square patch. Teflon material having dielectric constant of 2.1 and loss tangent of 0.0009 is chosen as a substrate for the work. At the operating frequency i.e at 39 GHz, the antenna exhibits a return loss and gain of $\mathbf{- 1 8. 3 8}$ dB and $9.838 \mathrm{~dB} \pm \mathbf{2. 3 \%} \mathrm{dB}$ respectively. The antenna’s radiation efficiency is noted as $\mathbf{8 6 \%} \pm \mathbf{1. 8 \%}$ the operating frequency. The overall size of the patch is $0.78 \lambda \times 0.78 \lambda$.

articleTitle: Attitude Controller Design for a Flying Wing UAV
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The simulation study plays a crucial role in making sure that the control strategies for autonomous operations of air vehicles could be developed and implemented in the most safe, efficient, and economical way possible. More specifically, this paper is focused on the modelling and controlbased simulation study for an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) named as Zagi flying wing. First-of-all, the short-period dynamics of the UAV is obtained from the rigid body equations of motion and further, it is represented in the state-space and transfer function models. Subsequently, a feedback control system is established for controlling the pitch attitude of the UAV by considering the controller, actuator, UAV dynamics, sensor, etc. in the loop. Here, the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) based control action is chosen due to its simplicity, reliability, robustness, and easy implementation on the hardware. A separate study is also conducted by considering P, PI, PD, and PID based control actions in controlling the pitch attitude of the UAV. The comparative analysis of these controllers in the simulation study reveals the appropriate choice for controlling the attitude dynamics of the UAV in the present analysis. It is also evident from this study that the UAV simulation is crucial in enhancing the control methodologies while offering a deeper insight into the UAV’s performance.

articleTitle: Demand Forecasting And Load Management For HT Consumer With Renewable Energy Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: IN Discom industrial and commercial HT consumer are charge by the high tariff rate and day by day it is increase. Government also initiate the renewable energy installation with different policy on rebate in tariff. So how can HT consumer get the proper benefit with installation of solar energy without increase their contract demand? As well as beneficial in financial way that present in this paper with case study and analysis of one HT consumer. In this case study solve many problems related to load demand, tariff policy, payback period, installation cost of solar power plant, participate in green energy power generation etc.

articleTitle: Hybrid Renewable Energy Source Based Shunt Active Power Filter To Analyze the Power Quality in A Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The progressive rise of integration techniques in the modern power systems invites some issues in the systems such as stability, reliability and power quality. This paper presents power quality analysis of such a system and its solution using a Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF), the proposed SAPF is fed through a hybrid Renewable Energy Source (RES) based Photovoltaic (PV) and Wind Energy (WE) hybrid system. Implementation of Proportional Integral (PI) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) controller combined techniques is used to regulate the DC link voltage across the capacitor of the voltage source inverter to obtain the accurate reference signal with synchronous reference method. Switching action is carried out by comparing the actual load signal to the reference signal. MATLAB Simulink platform is used for the proposed work and the effectiveness of different operating condition of the system is verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Human Crime Anomaly Detection using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The research focuses on developing an automated Human crime action recognition system using hybrid deep learning models to classify various anomalous human crime activities from real-time videos. We have used UCF-Crime dataset that contains 13 classes of anomalous activities and normal videos class, the research work explores and compares the performances of various models like Resnet-50 combined with simple-RNN, GRU, LSTM with models from other similar studies. These models were trained for binary, 5 -class and 14 class classifications, outperforming others in all the three respective classes. Thus, the research demonstrates the potential of deep learning in enhancing surveillance security by automating the detection of various serious crime actions in real time, offering significant improvements over traditional methods of manual surveillance.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Strategies for Solar Integrated Office Parking Lots
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The environmental issues motivated the widespread usage of electric vehicles (EVs) across the world. However, the high penetration of EVs has also brought numerous operational, technical, and financial challenges. These issues can be resolved by using distributed energy resources such as solar energy for charging EVs. Moreover, a well-structured EV charging strategy can effectively utilize energy resources and reduce the charging burden on the grid. In this context, the study proposed three charging strategies for grid-connected solar-integrated office parking lots to align the EV charging demand with solar generation to reduce grid dependency, considering the seasonal variation of solar production. Further, the proposed strategies are compared with uncontrolled charging in terms of annual peak demand and energy imported and exported to the grid across all seasons.

articleTitle: Advanced Stealth Protection for Android Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: As mobile devices become essential tools in daily life, their vulnerability to malware and phishing attacks has surged, particularly within the Android ecosystem. Current security frameworks predominantly rely on static or dynamic detection techniques, each with inherent limitations. Static analysis involves examining an application’s code and permissions to identify potential threats. However, this method often falls short against obfuscated malware and zero-day exploits that can dynamically alter their behavior to avoid detection. Conversely, dynamic analysis captures an application’s behavior during runtime, but it is constrained by the requirement for real-world user interaction and can miss threats that do not exhibit malicious behavior in controlled environments.To address these limitations, this project introduces an innovative Android security application that integrates both static and dynamic detection mechanisms through a robust cloud-based architecture. The application employs the DL-AMDet architecture for deep learning-based malware detection, utilizing a combination of CNN-BiLSTM for static feature analysis and deep autoencoders for dynamic feature extraction. Additionally, it implements advanced phishing detection algorithms for both website URLs and SMS messages, utilizing machine learning techniques tailored for URL classification and SMS pattern recognition. By harnessing cloud resources, the system not only enhances performance and scalability but also provides comprehensive security coverage that adapts to emerging threats. This hybrid approach ultimately aims to fortify the Android user experience against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Monopole Antenna Design for Low Profile IoT and Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents the design of Dual-band compact microstrip patch antenna. The antenna was made of a material like FR-4 as a substrate and copper for the patch and ground. The design has a resonating frequency of $2.373 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ and 2.673 GHz for many small scale applications, and industrial applications with some significant Transmission characteristics. The proposed antenna was fabricated using a $30 \times 30 \mathrm{~mm}$ FR4 material substrate. This antenna has good characteristics for IoT communications, which is light weight and small in profile making its fabrication cost-effective as fabrication process easy. The height of the substrate is taken 1.5 mm as per consideration of bands and return losses. The design modeling incorporates highend simulation techniques using microwave CST Studio, allowing for the optimization of key performance metrics, including directivity, gain, and efficiency.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics for Stock Market Price Using LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The stock market is a dynamic and complex financial system that poses significant challenges to researchers and investors due to its inherent randomness. Predicting stock prices is particularly difficult because of the numerous uncorrelated and volatile features involved, which often exceed the capabilities of traditional statistical methods. This paper presents a state-of-the-art machine learning model utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to predict stock prices. Leveraging historical stock data—including opening and closing prices, high and low values, and trading volumes—the proposed model captures temporal dependencies essential for time series forecasting. The study employs a comprehensive dataset spanning nearly a decade, coupled with systematic preprocessing to ensure data accuracy. The LSTM model is implemented using Python libraries for the stock prices of three large-cap companies listed on the NSE of India. Its predictive performance is validated through metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). This study not only demonstrates the efficacy of deep learning for stock price forecasting but also paves the way for incorporating additional factors, such as sentiment analysis and macroeconomic indicators, to enhance real-time applications. By leveraging artificial intelligence (AI), the model offers data-driven insights to support informed trading decisions.

articleTitle: Non-Unit Protection Scheme Assessment of Stand-Alone PV Generating System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Due to recent energy policies and increased rate of global warming, to curtail the impact of greenhouse gas emissions, a source like solar plays an important role in power generation but it is affected by irradiance, temperature (which changes due to changing atmospheric conditions) and load. As PV array has a unique point depending on both temperature and irradiation, where the generation of power, is maximum, an optimum algorithm is necessary to implement. To get optimal power under all possible conditions, the maximum power point (MPP) must be accurately tracked. In this proposed work, the performance of Perturb & Observe (P&O) algorithm is analyzed. Depending on local geographical location, the simulation parameters of proposed model are taken. Here, different types of protection schemes incorporated with relay system are provided in the power system network. The primary aim of these schemes is to detect faults in the network and to isolate the faulted part from the remaining healthy system. The protective relays continuously monitor the power system and operate when any quantities deviate from their normal levels. In this work, the impedance type relay is considered for the test model for detection of faults and the protection of the system. The results of proposed system are analyzed and verified using MATLAB/Simulink software. It is found that the proposed scheme works effectively under all adverse situations like fault, irradiance etc.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Albedo effect on Bi-facial Module Configuration for Mega Solar PV Plant
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The performance and efficiency of PV modules is dependent on various factors such as solar irradiance, temperature, humidity, soiling and module losses. Further, the reflections from the ground surface on the rear side of Bi-facial solar panels can improve power generation compared to standalone Mono-facial solar panel modules. Therefore, the surface of the ground is important in analyzing the power improvement and performance of Bi-facial solar modules. This paper analyzes the albedo effect on a Bi-facial module configuration for different reflecting surfaces for a large scale mega solar power plant. The study also focuses on evaluating the performance and feasibility of Bi-facial and Mono-facial configurations in terms of performance ratio, loss factor, module losses and energy yield. Comparison with three reflecting surfaces such as Urban Environment, Grass and Fresh Snow shows that the performance ratio and energy yield of Fresh Snow are better compared to others.

articleTitle: A New Eleven Level Switched Capacitor Multilevel Inverter with Reduced Power Semi Conductor Devices and Sources
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper proposes an eleven-level switched capacitor multilevel inverter to minimize the number of devices and voltage sources. The proposed topology uses two DC voltage Sources, a capacitor, eight power semiconductor switches, and a diode to produce the eleven level voltage at the inverter’s output terminals. The key features of the proposed inverter are the capacitor’s self-voltage balancing capability and requirement of less number of sources. The voltage magnitude across the switched capacitor depends up on the modes of the eleven-level inverter. Also, the device has less voltage stress. Also, the topology has the less switching losses and less ripple in capacitor voltage. To evaluate the system’s performance, MATLAB/Simulink simulations are carried out to study and verify the system’s behavior.

articleTitle: Integration of Green Hydrogen Production with Water Desalination: A Sustainable Path Forward
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Growing concerns over climate change have underscored the urgency of identifying clean energy sources to ensure a sustainable future. Energy security is also a key priority for emerging economies. Green hydrogen has recently gained significant attention as a potential energy solution. One method of producing green hydrogen is through water electrolysis powered by renewable energy (RE). However, currently, only about 4% of global hydrogen production comes from this green method. This process requires ultrapure water for the electrolyzers, making cost-effective water treatment essential for green hydrogen production. This review highlights importance of low-cost, high-recovery water desalination (WD) and distillation technologies, such as membrane desalination (MD) and multi-effect distillation (MED) and its integration in green hydrogen production system. It explores the integration of water desalination with green hydrogen production as a pathway toward sustainable development. Ensuring a reliable supply of sustainable water is crucial for scaling up green hydrogen production. Large-scale green hydrogen production could strain freshwater resources, which are needed for drinking, agriculture, and industry. The abundant seawater offers a potential solution, provided desalination can be made more affordable and sustainable. Therefore, desalination and distillation technologies will be central to the future hydrogen economy. This review aims to provide an overview of potential sustainable solutions to the interconnected challenges of hydrogen energy and water availability.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis and Detection of Wildfire Impact onVegetation and Wildlife and Biomass Emission
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Wildfires pose severe threats to ecosystems, biodiversity, and public safety, necessitating precise and efficient detection systems. While existing algorithms like YOLO and Mask R-CNN are commonly used, they struggle with predicting complex fire zones and evaluating ecological impacts. This study introduces a novel wildfire detection application using a modified U-Net model, leveraging satellite imagery for accurate fire forecasting. It integrates synthetic datasets to assess wildlife impacts, such as habitat loss and species vulnerability, and estimates vegetation loss through NDVI analysis. Furthermore, it calculates CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions and equivalent daily outputs to quantify environmental impact, thus helping policymakers to come up with effective wildfire management strategies. The approach thus provides a holistic and innovative solution to the monitoring of wildfires by dealing with ecological disturbances along with fire detection.

Author Keywords: NDVI is the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index

articleTitle: Queueing Network Analysis for Electric Vehicle Management Systems using G-Queues
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This study introduces an advanced queueing model for electric vehicle (EV) charging stations that incorporates negative and positive arrivals, representing various system disruptions and service interruptions. The research addresses the growing complexity of EV charging infrastructure by developing a comprehensive mathematical framework using G-queue networks and modified Chapman-Kolmogorov differential-difference equations. We analyze system performance through multiple system performance metrics, including expected waiting times, queue lengths, and server utilization patterns under the influence of negative arrivals. The model incorporates key operational parameters such as positive and negative arrival rates, service completion rates, and the probability of negative customer impacts on the system state. Through numerical analysis, we demonstrate the significant impact of these parameters on system stability and resource utilization. Results reveal that managing the balance between regular service provision and handling negative customer disruptions can substantially improve overall system reliability. The findings provide valuable insights for EV charging station operators, enabling them to implement robust operational strategies that account for various forms of service interruptions and system perturbations.

articleTitle: Optimization of Power in Power Converters Using Machine Learning: An Overview
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The rapid evolution in power electronics have brought significant attention to the optimization of power converters, which are essential for efficient energy conversion and management. Traditional techniques for optimizing power converters often struggle with the increasing complexity of modern systems, including nonlinear dynamics, diverse operating conditions, and stringent efficiency requirements. Last few decades, it has been observed that machine learning has evolved as hopeful solution with data driven methodologies to address various challenges. This survey provides the integration of machine learning for optimizing power converter, reviewing new approaches, key procedures and application in different domain. This categorizes different types of machine learning techniques and evaluate their usage in multiple fields like real-time control, fault detection, thermal management and system design. The paper also discusses different datasets, evaluation metrics and implementation framework in field of power converters. Lastly, challenges like computational complexity, data security and real-world deployment are highlighted along with direction towards future research to enhance the integration between machine learning and power converters. The comprehensive review aims to provide insight of researchers carried out to develop an intelligent power system.

articleTitle: Smart Solar Panel Maintenance: A Data-Driven Approach Using IoT and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents a solution for optimizing solar panel maintenance through a simple Arduino-based cleaning system. The system utilizes sensors to monitor environmental factors and trigger automated cleaning as needed. Additionally, a machine learning (ML) model forecasts future conditions and predicts cleaning requirements based on historical data, ensuring proactive maintenance that minimizes downtime and maximizes energy production. The paper demonstrates how this Arduino-based smart cleaning system is more efficient than manual cleaning of solar panels. It details the system’s design, implementation, experimental results, and economic implications, highlighting benefits such as reduced labor costs, lower water consumption, and increased energy efficiency. Furthermore, the paper discusses potential future advancements, including enhanced sensor integration and AI-powered tracking capabilities.

articleTitle: A web application for emmission reduction in coal mining
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This research presents a novel system, called as EcoMineInsight, designed to calculate the carbon footprint of coal mining operations in India and recommend effective remedial measures using machine learning (ML) models. The system integrates multiple carbon footprint calculators to evaluate the environmental impact of coal mining activities, providing users with a comprehensive assessment of their carbon emissions. By leveraging data and advanced ML algorithms, the system analyzes the results and offers personalized recommendations to reduce emissions based on operational practices and technological improvements. This approach not only enhances the accuracy of carbon footprint calculations but also enables actionable insights for emission reduction strategies tailored to the specific needs of Indian coal mines. The research aims to provide an accessible, data-driven tool that supports the transition toward more sustainable mining operations, aligning with global efforts to mitigate climate change and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the mining industry.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance: A Review of Induction Motor Bearing Fault Detection and Prognostics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of induction motor bearing fault prediction methods, centering around the emerging Digital Twin approach for predictive maintenance. Traditional fault prediction methods, including signal processing, machine learning, and hybrid techniques, have laid the groundwork for bearing health monitoring but often face limitations in real-time adaptability and scalability. In contrast, Digital Twin technology creates a virtual replica of the motor, integrating real-time sensor data and advanced analytics to accurately estimate the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of bearings. By continuously updating the virtual model with operational data, the Digital Twin enhances the accuracy of fault detection and improves predictive maintenance capabilities. The integration of AI and machine learning with Digital Twin technology further boosts RUL predictions, offering potential benefits such as reduced downtime, improved reliability, and optimized maintenance schedules. This review highlights the advantages of the Digital Twin approach and suggests upcoming research prospects to expand its industrial application and improve operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact of Torque Ripple in PMSM on EV Energy Efficiency and Driving Range
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This comprehensive review explores the impact of torque ripple in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) on the energy efficiency and range of electric vehicles (EVs). PMSMs are widely used in EVs for their high efficiency and performance, but torque ripple, which refers to periodic fluctuations in the motor's torque output, can significantly degrade motor efficiency and vehicle performance. The review begins by providing an overview of PMSMs in EVs, defining torque ripple, and highlighting its significance in optimizing vehicle operation. The causes and types of torque ripple are thoroughly examined, including cogging torque, electromagnetic disturbances, and mechanical imperfections. The paper differentiates between low-frequency torque ripple, which affects vehicle vibration, and high-frequency ripple, which primarily leads to energy efficiency losses. Furthermore, the review discusses the negative impact of torque ripple on EV performance, focusing on increased energy consumption, accelerated battery degradation, and reduced regenerative braking efficiency, all of which contribute to a diminished driving range and overall vehicle longevity. Finally, the review presents the latest strategies for mitigating torque ripple, including advanced motor control techniques such as Model Predictive Control (MPC), Adaptive Direct Torque Control (DTC), and optimized inverter design. These methods offer effective solutions for reducing torque ripple, improving energy efficiency, and extending the range of EVs. This review provides a thorough understanding of the role of torque ripple in PMSMs and suggests practical approaches for minimizing its effects on EV performance.

articleTitle: Optimizing Critical Parameters Influencing Floating Solar PV System Performance Using Response Surface Methodology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Solar PV systems, essential for achieving UN Goal 7 on Affordable and Clean Energy, face land constraints, particularly in densely populated areas, which can be mitigated by deploying floating solar PV. The nascent development stage of floating PV systems poses challenges for performance estimation due to the reliance on suboptimal parameters. To address this gap, the study examines critical parameters specific to floating PV systems and optimizes them using Response Surface Methodology, PVsyst simulations, and real-time monitored data from a 732 kW floating PV system. The performance ratio’s root mean square error was reduced to 3.889 by optimizing the parameters; the optimized values were supported by the particular system type and environmental factors. Building on prior findings, this study remarkably enhanced prediction accuracy of the tool by $\mathbf{4 0. 5 \%}$, challenging the assertion that no tool can accurately model floating PV systems. The methodology presented in this study allows stakeholders to evaluate and optimize critical parameters for such system type, thereby improving performance prediction accuracy and reducing both field measurement costs and time.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Traffic Signal Control Using Deep Q-Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Traffic congestion is a critical issue in urban areas, contributing to increased travel time, fuel consumption, and environmental pollution. Traditional traffic signal control methods, such as fixed-time systems, cannot adapt to real-time changes in traffic conditions. This paper presents a novel approach using Deep Q-Networks (DQN) to control traffic signals based on realtime traffic data dynamically. Our simulation environment models a four-way intersection, where vehicle densities and wait times are continuously monitored. The DQN agent optimizes green light durations by minimizing vehicle wait times and maximizing traffic throughput. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that our system significantly reduces congestion and improves traffic flow compared to traditional fixed-time systems. Furthermore, the approach shows potential for real-world applications in urban traffic control systems, particularly in smart cities equipped with Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

articleTitle: Applications of Sustainable Electric Vehicle Infrastructures Using Stochastic Threshold Strategies in Green Transportation and Highway Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This study presents a queueing-theoretic framework for single-server electric vehicle (EV) charging networks, utilizing threshold-based strategies to enhance EV network efficiency associated with green transportation. The approach incorporates stochastic modeling and Chapman-Kolmogorov equations to dynamically modify service rates when demand reaches predetermined thresholds, thereby minimizing waiting times and optimizing server utilization. Further, numerous system performance indicators are demonstrated to emphasize the efficiency and superior performance of EV charging infrastructures located on green highway networks. Further, numerical results illustrate the model’s efficacy in addressing critical operational issues, providing a practical framework to enhance EV network performance and customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in clean energy system using wavelet transform and machine learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The increasing integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into power grids brings challenges in ensuring reliability and stability due to various faults. This paper proposes a hybrid approach using wavelet transform (WT) and machine learning (ML) techniques to address these challenges. WT extracts key transient features from voltage and current signals, while ML classifiers such as Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) are employed for accurate fault detection and classification. The proposed method achieves high accuracy, demonstrated through simulations under diverse fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cybersecurity in Sustainable Energy: Regulatory Compliance, Challenges, and Policy Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The global switch to renewable energy is both a necessity for sustainable development and climate change mitigation. However, this transition is coupled with unique cyber security issues because of the greater reliance on networked digital systems. This paper identifies significant flaws in the current cyber security regulations and procedures while highlighting their effectiveness in the renewable energy sector. Recent research with the analysis highlighted the necessity of adaptable regulatory tools and the particular vulnerabilities that exist in renewable energy networks. According to the report, stronger regulations on the policymaking side must be enforced: rigorous regulatory compliance, increased robustness, and the incorporation of newer security practices that address changing threats. We explore how the integration of cutting-edge technology such as artificial intelligence (AI) could strengthen system resilience using current case studies like China’s renewable energy projects and Germany’s Energiewende. Furthermore, the importance of cybersecurity in the attainment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is evaluated based on how it supports environmental conservation, economic development, and renewable energy. This research will aid the stakeholders and policymakers in making a safe and sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Hilbert spectral analysis for PQ disturbances detection in Sustainable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: As the integration of renewable energy sources into power grids increases, ensuring power quality in sustainable energy systems has become a critical challenge. This paper presents a novel approach for identifying power quality (PQ) disturbances using Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT), a powerful time-frequency analysis tool. Unlike traditional Fourier-based methods, HHT is highly effective in analyzing non-linear and non-stationary signals, making it particularly suitable for complex power quality events such as voltage sags, swells, harmonics, and transients. The proposed method first applies Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to decompose the power signal into a set of intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), followed by the application of Hilbert spectral analysis to extract instantaneous frequency and amplitude features. These features are used to identify and classify different types of disturbances in real-time. The performance of the Hilbert-Huang Transform is validated through simulations and case studies, demonstrating its superior ability to handle complex and timevarying power quality disturbances with higher accuracy compared to conventional techniques. This method offers significant improvements in both diagnostic precision and computational efficiency, providing a robust solution for realtime power quality monitoring and disturbance mitigation in smart grids.

articleTitle: Forest Fire Severity Detection using AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Forest fires pose significant threats to ecosystems and contribute to global warming. Assessing fire severity is crucial for effective firefighting and minimizing damage, typically relying on post-fire metrics. This study addresses real-time forest fire severity assessment, crucial for minimizing fire damage. We propose a method combining deep learning and weather data. Fire severity was then estimated by combining fire area (from image analysis), a visual fire distance rating, and the Fire Weather Index (FWI) from weather data. Various optimizing techniques are used on a formulated weighted average equation such as Genetic algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, and Quasinewton method (QN) for finding the optimized weights that minimizes the Mean Square Error (MSE) between assigned and calculated severity scores. Interestingly, the FWI received the highest weight, while the fire area received the least, highlighting the importance of weather data alongside image analysis.

articleTitle: Enhanced Road Defect Detection with Deep Learning: Integrating Surface Texture Analysis and Background Subtraction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Maintenance of roads is necessary for the enhancement of safety standards and reduction of overall costs incurred from using a vehicle. Fusing computer-aided techniques to high-resolution photography allows for a more accurate assessment of the condition of the road. This research presents a new approach in the classification of imperfections found on a road’s surface to optimize the upkeep of the said road. It utilizes texture analysis along with the removal of the backdrop. Accroding to the research, MobileNetV2 and VGG16 net deep learning models are accurate at classifying the condition and type of surface a road has. The comparison provided some fascinating data. Transformation of maintenance procedures with the use of advanced maintenance is now possible because of how these models outperform existing methods. Claiming the use of light weight deep learning models for the preliminary assessment of road surface over standard models improves accuracy by more than five percent has proven changes in the framework and metric associated to the identification and diagnosis of issues concerning the quality of the surface to be more concentrated. This analysis will ultimately yield more effective maintenance programs. This is what will make road, infrastructure safer and more durable.

articleTitle: Analysis of Parameters Influencing Electric Vehicle Range, Velocity, Acceleration & Battery Capacity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The range, velocity, acceleration, and battery capacity of electric vehicles (EVs) are crucial factors influencing their performance and consumer appeal. With the rapid advancements in EV technology, manufacturers are introducing models with varying motor types, body structures, and battery configurations, making it challenging for consumers to compare and select the most suitable option. This study analyzes the key parameters affecting EV performance by simulating different configurations using MATLAB’s Simulink and Simscape tools. The Electric Vehicle Simulator models essential components such as drive cycles, motor controllers, DC motors, gearboxes, and vehicle bodies to evaluate their impact on overall performance. By systematically comparing simulation results, this research provides insights into how these factors influence EV efficiency, enabling consumers and manufacturers to make more informed decisions regarding electric vehicle selection and optimization.

articleTitle: MongoDB in the Era of Big Data Architecture, Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The emerging field of Big Data analytics has sparked the development and application of several procedures, technologies, structures, and fields by researchers worldwide beneficial to assess the gigantic amount of data which is produced on the daily basis. The enormous volumes of data that comprise “Big Data” are difficult for traditional database management systems to process. The Big Data architecture that can be used to address the issues the Big Data industry is currently facing is described in this paper. We also briefly discussed about the Opportunities as well as Big Data’s Challenges from an Analytical and Storage Perception. An overview and quick comparison of four different kinds of databases have been provided in this document. This study also aims to demonstrate the significance of MongoDB database which provides an efficient means of addressing Big Data issues and potential future developments.

Author Keywords: Ingestion of Messages in Real Time

articleTitle: Optimal Green Energy Estimation for Sustainable Electric Vehicle Networks Using Queueing-Based Retrial Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents a stochastic model for addressing a single-server service station offering both EV charging and battery swapping services, considering the realistic retrial-based queueing behavior of the waiting individuals. A computationally efficient method is proposed for determining the steady-state probability distribution of the charging network. The approach involves analyzing the governing differential-difference equations and employing a matrix method to derive the steady-state probability distribution. Further, straightforward formulae are derived for critical system performance indicators, considering both server and system characteristics. Numerical results are visualized in the form of different graphical representations to demonstrate the influence of various parameters on system performance. Finally, the paper concludes with significant findings and future research directions to apprise researchers, decision-makers, and system designers in optimizing combined charging/swapping infrastructure.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning for Solar Energy Forecasting: A Comparative Study of BGRU and T-BGRU Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Achieving accurate predictions of solar energy is a critical requirement for reliable operation of modern power grids. In the current work, we introduce a comparative analysis of Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BGRU) and Transfer Learning-BGRU (T-BGRU) models for short-term solar energy forecasting over the Maharashtra-Mumbai region, with Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI) as the main predicted variable. By transferring the knowledge, significant improvement was observed concerning Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (nRMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Standard Deviation with the T-BGRU model as compared with the standard BGRU model. Perfect MAE of 0.001444 and nRMSE of 0.0155 was achieved using the T-BGRU model. This infers that the T-BGRU offers more accuracy and predictability. Most importantly, the generalization capability of the T-BGRU model proves it to be more than ideal for real-time applications in forecasting solar resources. Thus, these results demonstrate the feasibility of applying transfer learning for enhanced performance of models, especially when training data is limited to certain localities or conditions.

articleTitle: An Enhanced and High-Performance Algorithm for Accurate Named Entity Recognition in Legal Text
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The rise of digital technologies results in the generation of large volumes of legal data. Although natural language legal texts are easily understood by humans, they pose significant challenges for machine processing. Converting this information into a machine-readable format is essential for efficient legal data analysis. In this paper, we propose resource-efficient method for extracting and classifying named entities within legal documents. We use rule-based learning and regular expressions to identify legal entities like parties, courts, and case references. Once extracted, these entities are classified into categories such as individuals, legal organizations, and jurisdictions. To improve both accuracy and processing speed, we implement a modified K-Means algorithm clustering the extracted entities. This clustering step refines the classification by grouping entities based on their shared attributes. The proposed method significantly enhances the speed and precision of Named Entity Recognition (NER) for legal texts, enabling faster and more efficient legal data processing.

articleTitle: Autonomous Intelligence: AI’s Role in Transforming Vehicles, Drones, and Space Missions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has transformed industries by enabling autonomous capabilities in self-driving cars, unmanned aerial vehicles, and spacecraft. This comprehensive analysis examines the AI architectures employed in these domains, their impacts, challenges faced during deployment, and future potential. AI has revolutionized decision making for self-driving cars, especially concerning steering assistance and safety features, addressing both technical and practical issues. For unmanned aerial vehicles, AI has boosted autonomy across uses, such as monitoring, mapping, and transportation, diminishing human intervention while improving work productivity. Although spacecraft autonomy remains in the early phases, AI is positioned to revolutionize deep-space missions by allowing autonomous fault tolerance, route planning, and determination, confronting problems such as communication delays on distant missions. The merging of AI with these technologies paves the way for a new era of autonomous systems in diverse fields.

articleTitle: Performance Investigation of Electric Vehicle Charging Network Using FES and SOS Service Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The article presents an advanced queueing framework for electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructures that integrate second-optional services (SOS), such as cleaning and maintenance, with first-essential services (FES), namely battery charging and battery swapping. Through the process of employing the matrix method and Chapman-Kolmogorov differential-difference equations, the investigation establishes a thorough statistical framework to address the increasing complexity of the EV charging network. Several measures, such as expected system and queue length, anticipated waiting times, and overall system throughput, are envisaged for evaluating system performance. The model includes critical operational characteristics, including arrival rates, service completion times, and the likelihood of individuals acquiring optional services following the completion of essential services. Through computational analysis, we demonstrate the significant impact of system design parameters on system performance and resource utilization. The outcomes indicate that overall system performance can be significantly improved by controlling the proportion between essential and optional services and optimizing service procedures.

articleTitle: Impact of Deep Learning Techniques on Automated Sleep Staging Diagnosis using BrainEEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Sleep, a fundamental physiological process, manifests as a cascade of changes in brain waves, muscle tension, eye movements, and heart and respiratory activities. Monitoring and analyzing sleep and sleep patterns is thus essential for understanding their impact on physical, mental, and emotional health. Traditional methods, exemplified by polysomnography (PSG) and Actigraphy, have long been the gold standards for sleep staging diagnosis but suffer from high costs, subjectivity in data interpretation and patient discomfort. Deep learning (DL), a subset of artificial intelligence, has lately emerged as a transformative force in sleep analysis. This paper comprehensively examines state-of-the-art DL models like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) evaluating their exceptional potential to classify sleep stages accurately. The literature survey encompasses studies of various physiological signals through Electroencephalogram (EEG), Electrooculogram (EOG), Electromyogram (EMG), and Electrocardiogram (ECG) for automated sleep staging. Model performances are compared across multiple datasets like SleepEDF, SHHS, and PhysioNet, showeasing high classification accuracies-often exceeding 85%—when leveraging hybrid models with multimodal inputs. Key findings indicate that CNN and hybrid models offer high classification accuracy, particularly when multiple signals are utilized. Despite these advancements, challenges such as data quality, interpretability, and generalizability persist. The findings suggest that DL holds immense promise for improving diagnostic accuracy, scalability, and accessibility in sleep research. Furthermore, this review helps to identify open challenges and opportunities for future research, emphasizing the integration of personalized medicine and cloud-based healthcare solutions.

articleTitle: A New Technique for Monitoring and Protection of Distribution Transformer during Single-Phasing Situation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The distribution transformer serves a significant purpose in the existing distribution grid. The distribution transformer may quickly switch from a three-phase to a two-phase power source in the event of a phase disruption or blown fuse from the primary side. In this instance, the secondary voltages may differ from the nominal phase voltage where LT consumers are connected. This is because the total secondary voltage depends on the actual primary voltages. This indicates that one voltage stays at the nominal level, but the other two do not. The magnetic permeability in each core limb, ampereturns, and core size all affect the voltage induced on the secondary side. The complex interactions between the elements above are considered when calculating these voltages using a comparable magnetic circuit. Under the worst unbalanced voltage condition on the secondary side due to single phasing on the primary side, this results in severe heating, power quality issues, losses, and transformer failure. Hence, this paper proposes a protection scheme against the single phasing condition of the transformer in the distribution system. An overvoltage relay, connected to the open delta-connected PT secondary detects the unbalance voltage condition on the distribution system.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Object Detection for Humanoid Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: In the contemporary world, humanoid robots are likely to play a key role in various fields, including health care, domestic service, hospitality, business, and military and security activities. The robots are employed to assist people in accomplishing specific missions or sometimes substitute human beings in hazardous situations. To accomplish these missions effectively, humanoid robots should be very good at recognition and subsequent processing of objects. The main goal of this research is to enhance the object recognition capabilities Leverage the advancements in deep learning to provide the control of Robotis-Op3 humanoid robots. In this work, the researchers analyzed popular deep neural models, among which are VGG16 and ResNet, highly promoted for their robust object recognition ability, as well as the more recent CNN architectures such as SSD MobileNetV3. This research improves object recognition capabilities on hu-manoid robots as such to enhance performance. in different domains, allowing them to better recognize and interact with the objects around them. This development will then allow more efficient and effective utilization of humanoid robots, extending their application and contribution in society.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Medical Imaging: CNN-Based Approach for Multi-Class Brain Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Brain tumors rank as one of the most serious and potentially fatal conditions and the importance of early detection in addressing the ailment cannot be overlooked. Our research paper proposes a technology-enhanced approach to brain tumor classification using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to ease the work of healthcare providers by providing them with effective tools for diagnosis. Based on MRI images obtained from the Kaggle database, this research aims to classify brain tumors correctly into four classes Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary, and No Tumor. The proposed CNN has an architecture that consists of several convolutional layers for full-feature extraction and two fully connected layers for fine classification. The model employed categorical cross-entropy as the loss function and accuracy as the benchmark measure of performance. Training versus validation accuracy and loss graphs were also generated to assess the performance, stability, and generalization of the model. Our paper addresses the medical imaging processing in improving the diagnosis accuracy which is also a step forward towards the development of automated tumor detection systems. In the model that we have developed and implemented, we were able to achieve an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6. 5 6 \%}$ and thus believe that it will be useful for automated medical diagnosis and can assist doctors in many different ways.

articleTitle: Field Performance Assessment of a 1.34 kW Rooftop PV plant in Delhi: Insight from two Comparative Periods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
