abstract: India’s growing energy demands and focus on energy security highlight the potential of SPV plant. With abundant solar resources, the country is well-positioned to harness solar energy for sustainable development. This study evaluates the performance of a 1.34 kW SPV system at Delhi Technological University, analyzing data from February to August in 2023 and 2024. Key metrics include energy generation, performance ratio $(P R)$, capacity factor (CF), and system efficiency. Results show higher energy generation, PR, and CF in 2023 due to better solar irradiation and lower temperatures, while 2024 performance declined under reduced solar irradiation and higher ambient temperatures. These findings underscore the impact of local environmental conditions on PV efficiency and highlight the need for continuous monitoring of rooftop systems in urban settings like Delhi. Insights from this study support policymakers in optimizing renewable energy integration and meeting solar capacity targets.

articleTitle: Real-time Collision Detection and Traffic Congestion Control for Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Living in a world in touch with technology, one is plagued by various ambiguities. These problems can all find a home within computer vision and intelligent communication systems. One such difficulty is the recognition of traffic accidents on roads and mitigating the accumulation of semi-autonomous vehicles at the site via quick vehicle-to-vehicle communication. This paper presents a real-time collision detection and traffic congestion control algorithm for vehicular networks. YOLO $\mathbf{v}$ 8 (You Only Look Once - version - 8), the computer vision technology that plays its strings in capturing and detecting collision between two approaching vehicles works on a precision scale of achieving an accuracy of up to $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$. On the other hand, after the accident has been detected, the Path Optimization Algorithm (POA) assists in neutralizing traffic with a negligible delay at the points of congestion and directs them toward the best possible path through the concepts of graph theory. Via these two techniques upon its belt, the proposed technique deals with the presented problem in an efficient way. The efficacy of the proposed scheme is verified by comparing it with shortest path Dijkstra method and random path allocation algorithm using extensive simulation results.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Solar Energy Generation Techniques in Maharashtra Using Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The growth of sustainable energy solutions around the globe is making solar energy one of the most preferred sources of energy than other conventional sources like coal especially in countries like India where coal is still the mainstay of electricity generation. Since the generation of solar energy is subject to weather, geolocation, and time, in order to assimilate solar energy into the power grid, its forecasting needs to be done with a high level of accuracy. This paper provides a methodological framework utilizing Machine Learning (ML) on solar energy generation prediction models for the state of Maharashtra. This research aims to enhance the accuracy of solar power generation forecasting by leveraging historical weather data and advanced Deep Learning (DL) techniques, including and comparing the performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) models. The analysis takes into account the influence of different weather factors and applies different ML techniques enabling the model to make accurate estimates that increase efficiency and facilitate the smooth introduction of solar energy into the power system.

articleTitle: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Network and Explainable AI for Enhanced Pneumonia Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Advances in machine learning and computer vision have significantly improved the diagnostic capabilities of medical imaging. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have emerged as a crucial tool for image classification, particularly in detecting pneumonia from chest X-ray images. Despite their high accuracy, CNNs face challenges in clinical adoption due to their lack of interpretability. Medical practitioners require a clear understanding of the decision-making process to trust AI-generated diagnoses. To address the aforementioned challenge, we propose pneumonia classification model incorporating CNN with a combination of the model and Grad-CAM, for enhanced interpretability. Grad-CAM visually outlines critical regions, influencing the prediction, so the clinician can easily confirm AI-based diagnoses with a more confident and credible approach. It is exclusively for pediatric pneumonia, an accurate and explainable machine for early interventions that can also work in resource-scarce regions. Our research uses a set of 5,863 pediatric chest X-ray images, divided into Pneumonia and Normal classes. The dataset was acquired from Guangzhou Women and Children’s Medical Center and divided into three subsets: training, validation, and test. By improving the accuracy and transparency of the diagnosis, this model can help bridge the gap between AI and the real world. This can help facilitate quicker and more reliable pneumonia diagnostics.

articleTitle: Resilience to Flux Walking in Isolated Converters: A Comparative Study of Voltage Doubler and Diode Bridge
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The effectiveness of a current-fed full-bridge boost converter, a voltage doubler (VD), and a diode bridge (DB) secondary circuit configuration are contrasted in this research. It assesses the consequences of flux walking and switching asymmetry. Uneven magnetisation of the transformer core, or switching asymmetry, causes flux walking and, in turn, can reduce converter performance. This is a typical problem in power electronics. This study shows that switching asymmetry has a major impact on converter efficiency, especially when the DB configuration is used, which is vulnerable to imbalanced magnetic flux and causes notable decreases in efficiency. Alternatively, when it comes to switching asymmetry, the VD arrangement is more resilient. Maintaining more stable converter performance in asymmetric switching conditions is helped by its inherent structure, which helps combat the impacts of flux walking. To increase efficiency and reliability, especially under less-than-ideal operating conditions, the results show that choosing the right secondary configuration is crucial in current-fed isolated converters.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy-Driven P2P Blockchain System for Tracking EV Performance and Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are the foundation of sustainable mobility, yet effective maintenance tracking and performance monitoring is still difficult, particularly in decentralized ecosystems. To fill these gaps, this study suggests a Sustainable Energy-Driven Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Blockchain System that combines blockchain technology, IoT-enabled EV systems, and renewable energy sources. The system lowers operating costs and minimizes the greenhouse effect by using sustainable energy sources like wind and solar to power blockchain nodes, EV charging stations, manufacturing, distributors and, service centers. The decentralized P2P blockchain network guaranteed transparent, immutable tracking of EV performance indicators and maintenance logs. The Istanbul Byzantine Fault Tolerance (IBFT) consensus method provides safe, effective, and energy-efficient transaction validation. EVs’ IoT sensors continually gather performance data, including mileage and battery health, which is then stored on the blockchain for computationally intelligent predictive maintenance. The Ethereum Smart contracts improve dependability and reduce administrative burdens by automating warranty monitoring, maintenance schedules, insuring renewal and, service provider communications. Furthermore, by offering verified service records, the blockchain makes ownership transfers easier and increases market trust for used EVs. In line with the objectives of smart cities and green technology, this integrated strategy promotes adopting sustainable energy and improves the lifetime, efficiency, and accountability of EVs.

articleTitle: A Closed-Loop Virtual Synchronous Generator for Enhanced Stability in Islanded Solar Power Systems: Advancing Sustainable Energy Transition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Traditional thermal power plants operate with high inertia with the rotating synchronous machines and seamlessly manage real time disturbances such as load and generation variation, electrical faults etc. Solar integrated isolated power networks, however suffer from low inertia in addition to weather dependent unpredictable intermittent generation. The traditional way of improving inertia includes physical deployment of DC motor and Synchronous generator set which is less efficient and costly. This paper revisits an alternative approach to solve this problem using Virtual Synchronous Generators (VSGs) to promote a sustainable renewable energy (Solar) based transition of power system networks. The work presents real time integration of solar operated power network with VSG to demonstrate improvement of transient stability and thus inertia virtually and efficiently. The work also shows that the virtual DC motor part of hardware in loop (HIL) system of VSG can be effectively used to regulate the performance of the real power network more efficiently by a closed loop VSG supported by a Proportional plus Integral plus Derivate (PID) controller. The whole work has been conducted in MATLAB SIMULINK primarily with encouraging results, motivating towards its hardware implementation.

articleTitle: Integration of smart Sensors and Machine Learning Algorithms for Automated Pest Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper presents a new IoT-based approach for agricultural pest control, incorporating machine learning techniques. Traditional pest monitoring methods are labor-intensive and often result in the overuse of pesticides. The proposed system solves this problem by predicting pest populations using environmental data collected via IoT sensors. We use random forest regression and random search cross-validation to predict pests and identify important factors. The system calculates the amount of pesticides based on forecasts, helping farmers optimize use and reduce environmental impact. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the system in terms of accurate prediction and optimal pesticide application, and thereby providing a scalable and cost-effective solution for sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Protection based on Fine-Tuning CatBoost Fault Classification Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Transmission line challenges are complex because they involve many different factors and are subject to significant fluctuations. These complexities make it crucial to implement precise protective measures. Effective protection ensures that electrical power flows without interruption. To address these challenges, a new classification algorithm is proposed, which is based on CatBoost. This algorithm works in conjunction with a Wavelet Transform-based decomposition system. These tools help in accurately assessing the condition of the transmission lines and responding to any issues that may arise. For practical application, the Indian standard system serves as the simulation model. This system operates at a voltage rating of 220 kV and spans a length of 120 km, with a frequency of 50 Hz. The decomposition frequency is set at 4 kHz, and to perform the Wavelet decomposition method, 80 samples are taken per cycle. A comprehensive data collection occurs within the transmission line using the MULTIRUN block of PSCADTM software. This software is instrumental in gathering the necessary data for analysis. The developed CatBoost algorithm is implemented in MATLAB, ensuring that hyperparameters are optimized for better performance. Once data is collected from PSCADTM, it is then imported into MATLAB for further processing. The CatBoost algorithm is employed to validate the data and assess the performance of the transmission line protection system. The results from this classification reveal that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms traditional methods in protecting transmission lines.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Multi-Level Inverter Suitable for Solar Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: The penetration of renewable energy resources into the energy sector is gradually increasing. The major goal of the proposed work is to eliminate harmonic distortion and power quality problems in the solar PV system by designing, developing, and testing an 11-level multilevel inverter with contemporary power electronic switches. The issue of power quality has been a popular area of study in recent years as a result of the increasing use of power electronics converters to process power in various facets of our lives. To achieve adequate efficiency, the voltage level is raised in proportion to the power level. The multilayer power converter is becoming more and more common. Multilevel converter topologies have two main benefits: they reduce electromagnetic interference by having minimal deformation in output waveforms and restricted voltage load on the switching electronics. This work presents results based on both simulation studies as well as measurements on developed hardware set-up.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Machine Learning Techniques in Sleep Staging Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: Sleep staging is a critical process in diagnosing and understanding various sleep disorders. Traditional manual scoring methods are time-consuming, subjective, and require significant expertise, prompting the exploration of automated systems powered by machine learning (ML). This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of ML techniques employed in sleep staging systems, focusing on their architectures, features, datasets, and performance metrics. We review various models, including traditional ML approaches. Key studies highlight innovations like feature extraction from multi-modal signals, including EEG, EMG, EOG, and respiratory data, to enhance classification accuracy across different sleep stages. Challenges such as dataset quality, generalization, interpretability, and computational cost are discussed, alongside recent advancements addressing these issues. The analysis underscores the potential of ML in automating sleep staging with high accuracy and efficiency while emphasizing the need for standardized datasets, interpretable models, and robust validation frameworks. This review aims to guide future research toward more reliable, scalable, and clinically applicable sleep staging systems

articleTitle: Enhancing AI Strategy in Checkers through Minimax and Alpha-Beta Pruning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Sustainable Energy Technologies and Computational Intelligence (SETCOM)
abstract: This paper focuses on artificial intelligence in the game of Checkers and thus looks to further advance strategic decision-making within AI game agents. This is a problem arising in developing computationally efficient AI to scan complex board states so that optimum moves may be selected. Alpha-Beta Pruning applied with the Minimax algorithm reduces the amount of computing that needs to be done when assessing any move, thus enabling its speed and strategic playing capabilities to be increased. Results will come out of experiments regarding the proficiency of AI in competitive environments with the benefits of more efficient play, strategic placement, and adaptability. In summing this up, this way leads toward the improvement in advanced algorithms to enhance the strategic capabilities of AI as in games, thus toward generating responsive high-performance game agents.
